age-calculator.description: Calculate age in years, months and days from a date of birth. See completed months and weeks, total days, and the countdown to your next birthday.
age-calculator.seoTitle: Age Calculator: Years, Months, Days & Next Birthday

sections.title: Calculate your age today or on a specific date
paragraphs: Enter your Date of birth and the Age on date, then select Calculate. For your age today, open the Age on calendar and choose Today; it uses the current date in your device’s time zone. You can also enter a past date or a future date to answer “How old was I then?” or “How old will I be?” The comparison date must be on or after the birth date.

The main result is calendar age: completed years, additional completed months and remaining days. The calculator also shows total elapsed days, completed calendar months, complete weeks with leftover days, and the next birthday on or after your chosen date. The initial dates are a worked example, so replace them before reading the result as your own age.

sections.title: Worked age example: 23 September 1998 to 15 June 2026
paragraphs: Someone born on 23 September 1998 is 27 years, 8 months and 23 days old on 15 June 2026. Enter Date of birth 1998-09-23 and Age on 2026-06-15 to reproduce the result. The year subtraction 2026 − 1998 gives 28, but the September birthday has not yet occurred in June.

Count 27 complete years to 23 September 2025, then eight additional months to 23 May 2026, then 23 days to 15 June. The full interval contains 10,127 days. Its next birthday is 23 September 2026, exactly 100 calendar days after the selected date.

table.caption: Different ways to describe the same example age
rows: Completed calendar periods plus the remaining days
Days from the birth date to the selected date

links.label: Enter the dates in Age on a date

sections.title: Watch completed years change at the birthday boundary
paragraphs: For a birth date of 15 June 2000, compare the three dates below. One elapsed day passes between each row, but the completed-year result changes only at the birthday. This is why subtracting birth year from comparison year can overstate someone’s age before their birthday.

The birthday countdown includes an anniversary on the selected date: it reads zero on 15 June. On 16 June, it points to the following year. The countdown is measured from Age on, which may be a historical or future date, not necessarily from today.

table.caption: One birth date, three neighboring comparison dates

sections.title: Understand age in months when the birth date is at month end
paragraphs: Calendar months do not all contain the same number of days. Finflo counts complete months from the original birth date. If that day does not exist in the target month, it uses that month’s final day. It then counts the days remaining after the latest complete-month anniversary.

A birth date of 31 January 2025 reaches one complete month on 28 February. Two complete months end on 31 March, so 30 March is still one month plus 30 days under this convention. The calculator keeps the original day as its reference instead of repeatedly adding a month to the previously shortened February date.

table.caption: Month-end counting for a 31 January 2025 birth date

sections.title: Check the February 29 birthday convention
paragraphs: For a February 29 birth, this calculator uses February 28 as the anniversary in a non-leap year and February 29 when that date exists. Both calendar age and the next-birthday countdown follow this same rule. It is a stated counting convention, not a determination of legal age or eligibility.

Gregorian years divisible by four normally have a February 29, but century years must also be divisible by 400. Thus 2000 is a leap year and 2100 is not. The table illustrates a person born on 29 February 2024; the 2028 anniversary returns to February 29 rather than staying on February 28.

table.caption: A leap-day birth across common and leap years

links.label: U.S. Naval Observatory: Gregorian leap-year rules
RFC 3339 Appendix C on Gregorian leap years

sections.title: Keep elapsed age separate from inclusive day counting
paragraphs: On the birth date itself, calendar age and elapsed days are both zero. On the following date, one day has elapsed. Counting every date on a list, including both endpoints, answers a different question and would give one for a same-date range. Use the Day Counter’s Include end date option when that is the count you need.

Weeks always contain seven days, so the complete-weeks result and leftover days can be checked against Total days. Months and years vary in length: dividing days by 30 or 365 does not recover the calendar-age breakdown. For example, 31 January to 28 February is one complete month here even though only 28 days have elapsed.

links.label: Count dates with an optional inclusive end date
Add or subtract calendar years, months and days

sections.title: Know what a date-only age result can establish
paragraphs: This tool uses Gregorian dates without a birth time or time zone. Its day count is calendar arithmetic; daylight-saving clock changes do not add or remove a calendar date. It therefore does not claim your exact age in hours, minutes or seconds. For elapsed time between known instants, keep both dates, clock times and zones, convert both endpoints to UTC, and use the Time Duration Calculator.

Use the applicable organization’s rules when an age affects enrollment, insurance or another eligibility decision. A Gregorian date calculation does not reproduce every administrative rule or other calendar’s age-counting system. Supported input years are 0001–9999; if the next birthday falls after year 9999, the age totals remain available and the birthday result is omitted.

links.label: Calculate a duration from dated clock times
Convert date-specific times between named zones
TC39: calendar dates independent of time zones

faqs.question: How do I calculate my age today?
faqs.answer: Enter your date of birth, open the Age on calendar and choose Today, then select Calculate. Today follows your device’s local time zone. Replace the illustrative starting dates before using the result as your own age.

faqs.question: Can I calculate my age on a past or future date?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enter the date you want in Age on. It may be before or after today, but it must be on or after your birth date. The birthday countdown is also measured from that selected date.

faqs.question: Why is my age not simply this year minus my birth year?
faqs.answer: Subtract one from that year difference if your birthday has not occurred by the selected date. For example, someone born on 23 September 1998 is 27, not 28, on 15 June 2026.

faqs.question: How can I find my age in months or weeks?
faqs.answer: Read Completed calendar months for the whole-month count, leaving the remaining days separate. Complete weeks and Days after complete weeks divide the total elapsed-day count by seven. Neither calculation assumes a 30-day month.

faqs.question: Why can age show one month and 30 days?
faqs.answer: Each month anniversary is anchored to the original birth date and shortened only when that day is absent from the target month. From 31 January 2025, one month ends on 28 February and two months end on 31 March. Therefore 30 March is one month plus 30 days.

faqs.question: What happens if I was born on February 29?
faqs.answer: Finflo uses February 28 as the anniversary in a non-leap year and February 29 in a leap year. Calendar age and the next-birthday countdown use that same convention. Check the relevant rules separately for an official eligibility decision.

faqs.question: Why does the birthday countdown show zero?
faqs.answer: The next-birthday result includes the selected Age on date. If that date is your birthday under the calculator’s anniversary convention, the countdown is zero. The following date points to the next year’s anniversary.

faqs.question: Does the age calculator count the birth date as day one?
faqs.answer: No. It measures elapsed calendar days, so the birth date compared with itself is zero days and the following date is one day later. Counting both endpoint dates is an inclusive counting task, available in the Day Counter.

faqs.question: Can a date of birth alone give an exact age in hours or seconds?
faqs.answer: No. Exact elapsed clock time also requires a birth time, comparison time and time-zone information. This calculator uses dates only and reports calendar periods and whole elapsed days.

date-calculator.description: Find days between two dates, add or subtract days, weeks, months or years, and count business days with your selected holidays.

faqs.question: How many days are between two dates?
faqs.answer: Subtract the starting calendar date from the ending date. For 1–3 January 2026, two days elapse. Include end date changes that forward count to three.

faqs.question: Does this count weekends?
faqs.answer: Between two dates includes every calendar day. Business-day methods exclude weekends according to their stated or selected workweek and subtract eligible holiday dates.

faqs.question: Why does adding one month not always add 30 days?
faqs.answer: Month lengths vary. The calendar-addition method changes the month and uses its final day if the original day number is unavailable.

faqs.question: Can I subtract dates or business days?
faqs.answer: Yes. Negative year, month, week or day quantities subtract intervals. Reversed start/end comparisons produce signed counts under the selected boundary convention.

faqs.question: Are public holidays included automatically?
faqs.answer: Standard business-day modes use only the holiday dates you supply. Custom modes offer explicit rules and a labeled preset; select and verify them for the calendar you need.

faqs.question: Will daylight saving change the date difference?
faqs.answer: No. Date-only modes compare Gregorian calendar dates without clock-time offsets. Use time-zone conversion and dated time calculations when you need elapsed hours between instants.

sections.title: Which date calculation should I use?
paragraphs: Choose Between two dates to measure a calendar interval. Choose Add or subtract time to find a date a specified number of years, months, weeks or days away; use negative values to subtract. Business-day modes count only the selected working days and exclude the holiday dates or calendar rules you choose.

sections.title: Date calculation examples
paragraphs: Calendar months have different lengths. Adding a month changes the calendar month and clamps an unavailable day to the end of that month; it does not add a fixed 30 days. The date-only modes do not use time zones or daylight-saving offsets.

table.caption: Examples using the Gregorian calendar
rows: January 1 to January 3, 2026; exclude end date
January 1 to January 3, 2026; include end date

sections.title: Check the workweek and holiday calendar
paragraphs: Standard business-day modes count Monday through Friday and exclude the holiday dates you supply. Custom modes let you choose working weekdays and the available holiday rules or presets. No preset represents every country, employer or local calendar, so check the selected exclusions before using a deadline.

links.label: Calculate hours and minutes between timestamps

sections.title: Why one month and 30 days can produce different dates
paragraphs: From 31 January 2026, adding one calendar month gives 28 February; adding 30 days gives 2 March. The Add or subtract time mode applies the combined year/month change first, clamps an unavailable day to month end, and then applies weeks and days. A month is a position in the calendar, not a fixed duration.

Clamping can make an operation non-reversible: 31 January plus one month is 28 February, but subtracting one month from 28 February gives 28 January. For recurring month-end events, keep the original scheduling rule rather than repeatedly using the shortened result as the next starting point.

links.label: RFC 3339 Appendix C on Gregorian leap years

sections.title: Add working days without counting the starting date
paragraphs: For a Monday–Friday calendar with no holidays, five business days after Friday 9 October 2026 is Friday 16 October. The counted dates are Monday 12 through Friday 16. If 12 October is entered as an excluded holiday, the result moves to Monday 19 October. This example does not assume that any particular country observes that holiday.

A deadline may use a different start-day, holiday or cutoff-time rule. Enter the relevant calendar explicitly and use the result as calendar arithmetic. A due-at-5-p.m. rule or a filing extension cannot be inferred from the dates alone.

links.label: Add business days with your holiday list

date-calculator.seoTitle: Date Calculator: Days Between Dates & Business Days

day-counter.description: Count elapsed calendar or business days between dates, with an end-date option and custom working-day and holiday controls.

faqs.question: Does day one include the start date?
faqs.answer: Elapsed-day mode measures the interval, while inclusive counting counts both endpoint dates for a forward range. Business-day range mode includes an eligible start date and follows your end-date choice.

faqs.question: Can I count Monday to Friday only?
faqs.answer: Yes. Standard Business days uses Monday–Friday. Custom business-day methods let you choose other working weekdays.

faqs.question: Why is my result negative?
faqs.answer: The end precedes the start. The sign preserves the direction of the comparison; swap the dates if you need the forward interval.

faqs.question: How do I exclude a holiday?
faqs.answer: Enter its date in the holiday list or select the relevant supported custom rule. A non-working date is excluded only once.

faqs.question: Can I count a full month as 30 days?
faqs.answer: Only if your task explicitly defines a fixed 30-day interval. Calendar months range from 28 to 31 days.

faqs.question: Is the result a legal deadline?
faqs.answer: It is a calendar count under the selected rules. Filing, contractual and administrative deadlines may use additional start-day, cutoff-time or holiday rules.

sections.title: Choose elapsed days or a count of calendar dates
paragraphs: Use Between two dates for the length of a calendar interval. The default measures how many date boundaries pass from start to end: a date compared with itself gives zero, and the next date gives one. Include end date adds the endpoint to a forward count.

A hotel stay, a list of attendance dates and a project deadline may therefore need different counting conventions even when the displayed dates match. Decide what is being counted before interpreting the number.

sections.title: Worked example: a three-date interval
paragraphs: From 1 June through 3 June 2026, two full calendar days elapse. Counting every date in that list includes 1, 2 and 3 June, giving three. This distinction also explains why a same-date inclusive range has one date rather than zero.

table.caption: Elapsed interval versus inclusive date count

sections.title: Business-day counting uses a workweek as well as dates
paragraphs: In standard Business days, the start date counts if it is a working day, while the end date is excluded unless selected. For Monday 8 June to Monday 15 June 2026 with no holidays, the default count is five; including the final Monday gives six.

Use Custom business-day count for a different set of working weekdays. An excluded holiday already falling on a non-working day is not subtracted twice. Supplied holidays should match the actual dates excluded by your organization, including any observed-day convention.

links.label: Choose working weekdays and holiday exclusions

sections.title: Find the date after a chosen number of working days
paragraphs: Add business days answers the inverse planning task: start from a date and move forward or backward through eligible dates. Unlike range counting, the starting date is excluded. Five working days after a Monday is the next Monday when all five weekdays are eligible.
For adding calendar months, use the Date Calculator. A 30-day interval does not always end on the same day of the next month, and a complete month does not always contain 30 days.

sections.title: Use calendar days separately from elapsed clock time
paragraphs: The day counter does not apply time zones or daylight-saving clock changes. A weekend containing a clock change still spans the same named calendar dates. If your task is to measure an exact number of hours, supply both times and resolve the time zones first.
Leap days are included whenever they occur inside the interval. Gregorian century years are leap years only when divisible by 400; this makes 2000 different from 2100.

day-counter.seoTitle: Day Counter: Calendar Days & Business Days

day-of-the-week-calculator.description: Find a date's weekday, day number within the year and ISO week, using Gregorian calendar and Monday-based ISO conventions.

faqs.question: Why does an ISO week show the previous year?
faqs.answer: ISO week-years follow complete Monday–Sunday weeks. A January date before the first ISO Monday can belong to the final ISO week of December’s year.

faqs.question: Is 1 January day zero or day one?
faqs.answer: It is day 1 in the day-of-year result. The elapsed interval from 1 January to itself is zero days, a different measure.

faqs.question: Does every year have 52 ISO weeks?
faqs.answer: No. Some ISO week-years have 53 weeks because their first and last week boundaries straddle calendar-year boundaries.

faqs.question: Can a leap year change my birthday’s weekday?
faqs.answer: Yes. A leap day changes the number of intervening days. Enter the exact target year instead of assuming a fixed annual shift.

faqs.question: Does this know local holidays?
faqs.answer: No. A weekday label is independent of public-holiday or working-day status. Use a custom business-day calendar for exclusions.

sections.title: Find the weekday for a complete Gregorian date
paragraphs: Enter the year, month and day to find its weekday, ordinal day of the year and ISO week. The year matters: a birthday falling on Monday one year usually shifts the next year, with leap days changing the shift across February.
This date-only calculation does not require a time zone. It identifies the calendar label of the entered date, rather than the weekday at a particular instant in several countries.

sections.title: Worked example: a year boundary can use the previous ISO year
paragraphs: 1 January 2021 was a Friday and the first day of calendar year 2021, but it belongs to ISO week 2020-W53. ISO weeks begin on Monday, and week 1 contains 4 January. A few dates near New Year can therefore carry an ISO week-year different from their calendar year.

table.caption: Three date labels near New Year

sections.title: Read day-of-year numbers without an off-by-one error
paragraphs: 1 January is day 1, not day 0. In a common year, 1 March is day 60; in a leap year it is day 61. The ordinal number labels the date, whereas the elapsed interval since 1 January is one day smaller.
Use the Day Counter when the task asks how many days have passed between dates. The weekday and ordinal labels do not themselves specify whether to include either endpoint.

links.label: Count the interval between two dates

sections.title: Check leap years and historical-calendar assumptions
paragraphs: The arithmetic uses Gregorian rules: years divisible by four are leap years except centuries not divisible by 400. Thus 29 February 2000 is valid, while 29 February 2100 is not. Invalid dates must be corrected before calculation.

Historical records may use a different calendar or a local adoption date for the Gregorian calendar. This tool does not convert a Julian-calendar record or reconstruct a jurisdiction’s historical calendar transition.

sections.title: A weekday does not establish whether a place is open
paragraphs: Friday, Saturday or Sunday can be a working day depending on the country, employer and service. Holidays and closures are separate from the mathematical weekday. Use a business-day calculator with the relevant workweek and exclusions for that question.

links.label: Find the weekday at a destination time

day-of-the-week-calculator.seoTitle: Day of the Week Calculator: Weekday & ISO Week

hours-calculator.description: Calculate hours between start and end times, subtract unpaid breaks and convert to decimal hours. Supports same-day shifts and shifts crossing midnight.

faqs.question: How do I subtract lunch?
faqs.answer: Enter the excluded lunch duration in Break to subtract, in minutes. Subtract it once and follow your own paid-break rules.

faqs.question: Can I calculate an overnight shift?
faqs.answer: Yes. In clock mode an earlier end is the next day. Use dates when a shift lasts a full day or more.

faqs.question: Is 8 hours 30 minutes the same as 8.30 hours?
faqs.answer: No. It equals 8.5 decimal hours. Decimal fractions of an hour must be multiplied by 60 to obtain minutes.

faqs.question: Why do equal start and end times give zero?
faqs.answer: Without dates, the tool cannot distinguish the same instant from the next day. Use the dated mode for 24 hours.

faqs.question: Does this apply overtime or payroll rounding?
faqs.answer: No. It measures the entered duration. Use Time Card for its explicit rounding and overtime options; those settings still do not establish a legal payroll policy.

faqs.question: Will it handle daylight saving automatically?
faqs.answer: No. Convert zoned endpoints to UTC first when you need physical elapsed hours across an offset change.

sections.title: Turn a shift into net hours
paragraphs: Enter the start and end clock times and the break to subtract in minutes. The calculation finds the clock-time difference and subtracts that break once. To include the whole interval, set the break to zero. An end earlier than the start is treated as the following day.

For a shift of 09:00–17:30 with a 30-minute excluded break, the gross interval is 8 hours 30 minutes and the result is 8 hours. Decide which breaks should be excluded under your own records; the calculator does not decide whether a break is paid.

sections.title: Compare breaks and overnight shifts
paragraphs: The same clock interval can have different net hours when you change the excluded break. In the example below, the overnight interval is interpreted as ending the next morning.

table.caption: Net hours under explicit break assumptions

sections.title: Convert minutes to decimal hours before multiplying by a rate
paragraphs: A duration of 7 hours 45 minutes is 7 + 45/60 = 7.75 hours. Writing 7.45 as a decimal means 7 hours 27 minutes. Multiply the decimal-hour value, not the hour:minute text, when estimating a cost.
At an illustrative rate of 20 per hour, 7.75 hours produces 155 before any additional pay rules or deductions. For several shifts and an explicit overtime assumption, use the Time Card Calculator.

sections.title: Use calendar dates for exactly 24 hours or longer
paragraphs: Matching clock times give zero in the clock-only mode, not one full day. For 09:00 on 1 June to 09:00 on 2 June 2026, select Between two dates and times. A multi-day interval cannot be reconstructed reliably from clock times alone.

The dated method does not have the clock-mode break field. Measure the whole dated interval there and account for any excluded periods separately; do not assume a break entered in another mode is carried across.

sections.title: Separate civil hours from time-zone transitions
paragraphs: These modes treat each civil day as 24 hours. They do not automatically shorten a spring-forward night or lengthen a fall-back night. For elapsed time across such a transition, resolve both local timestamps to UTC with the Time Zone Calculator and compare those UTC dates and times.

links.label: IANA: how time-zone rules are maintained

hours-calculator.seoTitle: Hours Calculator: Work Hours, Breaks & Decimal Time

time-duration-calculator.description: Calculate elapsed time between clock times or two dates and times. Get hours, minutes and decimal hours, with optional break subtraction for a single-day interval.

faqs.question: How do I calculate a duration overnight?
faqs.answer: Enter the clock times normally. If the end is earlier than the start, the calculator treats it as the following day. For example, 22:15 to 06:45 is 8 hours 30 minutes before any break is subtracted.

faqs.question: Why is 8 hours 30 minutes shown as 8.5 decimal hours?
faqs.answer: Thirty minutes is 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 hours. Decimal hours use fractions of an hour, while hours-and-minutes notation uses 60 minutes per hour.

faqs.question: Which mode should I use for an interval spanning several dates?
faqs.answer: Use Between two dates and times. The clock-time mode represents a single interval of less than 24 hours.

faqs.question: Is civil-time duration always the elapsed time between zoned instants?
faqs.answer: No. Daylight-saving transitions can change actual elapsed time. This mode does not apply timezone offsets or transition rules.

faqs.question: How many seconds are in 49.5 hours?
faqs.answer: 49.5 × 3,600 = 178,200 seconds. The same interval is 2,970 minutes.

faqs.question: Can I measure a trip across two time zones?
faqs.answer: Resolve the departure and arrival local timestamps to UTC, then enter those UTC dates and times in the dated duration mode. Subtracting destination clock readings directly can give the wrong result.

sections.title: How to calculate elapsed hours and minutes
paragraphs: Enter the start and end time. Leave Break to subtract at 0 to measure the complete interval; enter break minutes only when you want to exclude them. The result shows hours, minutes and seconds, plus decimal hours.
Decimal hours divide the remaining minutes by 60. For example, 8 hours 30 minutes is 8 + 30 ÷ 60 = 8.5 hours, not 8.30 hours.

table.caption: Clock-time examples; an end time earlier than the start is treated as the following day.

sections.title: Overnight intervals and durations longer than a day
paragraphs: Clock-time mode treats an earlier end time as the next day. Matching start and end times give zero elapsed time, not 24 hours. For an interval lasting a full day or several days, select Between two dates and times and enter both dates.

These calculations compare civil clock readings and treat each day as 24 hours. They do not apply timezone offsets or daylight-saving transitions. If your interval crosses such a transition, compare the corresponding zoned instants instead.

sections.title: Reproduce a duration that spans several dates
paragraphs: From 09:00 on 9 October 2026 to 10:30 on 11 October, two full civil days contribute 48 hours and the remaining interval contributes 1 hour 30 minutes. The result is 49.5 hours, or 178,200 seconds.
Enter both dates explicitly. Counting only the two clock readings would show 1.5 hours and omit the two intervening dates. A dated interval and a clock-only interval answer different questions.

table.caption: Break down the same multi-day interval

sections.title: Check the unit before using a duration in another formula
paragraphs: For speed, divide distance by hours when the desired result is distance per hour. For a per-second process, use seconds instead. An interval of 6 hours 4 minutes is 364 minutes, so its decimal-hour value is 364/60 ≈ 6.0667.
Round the final result rather than repeatedly rounding each intermediate interval. Small rounding differences can accumulate when many tasks, recordings or shifts are combined.

links.label: Use a duration in a speed calculation

sections.title: Handle repeated or nonexistent local times before subtracting
paragraphs: A local clock reading can be skipped when an offset moves forward, or occur twice when it moves backward. The duration form does not identify these cases because it does not take a named time zone. Resolve each endpoint in Time Zone Conversion first, choosing the intended occurrence when necessary.
Date-only differences, civil clock differences and elapsed time between UTC instants are separate measurements. Keep that distinction when comparing a schedule with a stopwatch recording.

time-duration-calculator.seoTitle: Time Duration Calculator: Hours, Minutes & Breaks

time-calculator.description: Add and subtract durations, evaluate supported time expressions or shift a civil date and time by an entered duration.

faqs.question: Can I add more than two times?
faqs.answer: Yes. Duration expression accepts a sequence of supported time quantities joined by plus or minus signs.

faqs.question: Does 1.5 hours mean 1 hour 50 minutes?
faqs.answer: No. Half an hour is 30 minutes. In hours:minutes:seconds form, ninety minutes is 1:30:00.

faqs.question: Can the result exceed 24 hours?
faqs.answer: Yes. A duration is a length of time, so it can be 51 hours or more without wrapping to a clock face.

faqs.question: Why is the result negative?
faqs.answer: The quantity subtracted exceeds the starting duration. The sign is retained rather than interpreted as an overnight clock interval.

faqs.question: How do I add one calendar month?
faqs.answer: Use Date Calculator. Duration arithmetic uses fixed units through days and does not treat a month as a fixed number of seconds.

faqs.question: Does date-time addition apply daylight saving?
faqs.answer: No. Convert the relevant timestamps with named time zones when offset transitions affect the elapsed interval.

sections.title: Choose duration arithmetic or a new date and time
paragraphs: Duration arithmetic adds or subtracts lengths of time such as 2:30:00 and 1:45:00. Add time to a date moves a starting civil timestamp. Duration expression combines several quantities with d, h, m and s units. Choose the method that matches the quantity you want back.

A duration can exceed 24 hours; a clock reading cannot identify its calendar day on its own. To measure the interval between two known endpoints, use the Time Duration Calculator rather than adding the displayed clock readings.

sections.title: Worked addition: carry 60 minutes into the next hour
paragraphs: Adding 2 hours 30 minutes and 1 hour 45 minutes gives 3 hours 75 minutes, which normalizes to 4 hours 15 minutes. The duration is 4.25 decimal hours or 15,300 seconds.
Use the arithmetic fields as hours:minutes:seconds. The hour component is not the same as a decimal fraction; enter 1:30:00 for ninety minutes.

table.caption: The same duration in different representations

sections.title: Write a mixed-unit expression without decimal-clock ambiguity
paragraphs: The expression 2d 3h + 45m - 30s combines 172,800 + 10,800 + 2,700 − 30 seconds. Its result is 186,270 seconds: 51 hours 44 minutes 30 seconds. In duration expressions, one day means 24 hours.

Use explicit units for each quantity and the supported plus/minus operations. This is a duration parser, not a general programming language or a calendar-month expression. For calendar months and years, use the Date Calculator.

sections.title: Cross midnight by attaching the date
paragraphs: Starting at 23:30 on 9 October 2026 and adding 2 hours 15 minutes gives 01:45 on 10 October. The date must advance when the added duration passes midnight. Negative quantities move backward through the calendar.
The date-time mode performs civil arithmetic without named time-zone rules. It does not predict the clock change at a destination or account for a daylight-saving transition.

sections.title: Check signs and retain enough precision
paragraphs: Subtraction can produce a negative duration when the second interval is longer than the first. That sign describes the direction of the difference; it is not an instruction to wrap around midnight. Wraparound belongs to clock-time interpretation, a different task.
When combining many intervals, keep the unrounded seconds or full time values until the final total. Rounding each task to the nearest tenth of an hour can change a billing or scheduling sum.

time-card-calculator.description: Total dated or weekly shifts, unpaid breaks and estimated pay, with configurable overtime and clock-punch rounding.

faqs.question: Can I enter several shifts on the same date?
faqs.answer: Yes in dated mode. Daily overtime aggregates shifts by their starting work date, so check overnight shift attribution.

faqs.question: Does it automatically deduct lunch?
faqs.answer: No. Enter the break minutes to exclude. A zero break leaves the whole shift interval counted.

faqs.question: Is the amount net pay?
faqs.answer: No. It is estimated gross pay from hours, rate and the selected overtime calculation, before withholding and other deductions.

faqs.question: Can I turn overtime off?
faqs.answer: Use No overtime in dated mode when all counted hours should use the entered base rate.

faqs.question: Why does punch rounding change my hours?
faqs.answer: The selected increment rounds the start and end separately. That differs from rounding one final duration after subtraction.

faqs.question: Does this establish my legal overtime entitlement?
faqs.answer: No. Use the applicable employment rules and records to choose inputs; the form does not assess legal coverage or combine every pay rule.

sections.title: Build a time card from net shift hours
paragraphs: Weekly time card accepts one start time, end time and break in minutes per line, separated by commas. An example line is 09:00,17:30,30, meaning an 8.5-hour clock interval with a 30-minute excluded break: eight net hours. Enter the hourly rate and overtime assumptions separately.

Dated shifts & overtime provides rows with work dates plus explicit daily, weekly or no-overtime modes and punch-rounding settings. Use that method when the distribution of hours across dates matters, rather than entering only a weekly total.

sections.title: Work through a configurable overtime example
paragraphs: Suppose five shifts each run from 09:00 to 18:00 with no excluded break. Total time is 45 hours. With an assumed threshold of 40 hours, rate 20 per hour and multiplier 1.5, regular pay is 40 × 20 = 800 and overtime pay is 5 × 20 × 1.5 = 150. Estimated gross pay is 950.
These are chosen arithmetic assumptions, not a statement that every worker or country uses the same threshold or overtime rate. Change the inputs to match the rule you are applying.

table.caption: Forty-five-hour example at an entered rate of 20

sections.title: Distinguish daily overtime from weekly overtime
paragraphs: A day containing ten hours can create overtime under an eight-hour daily assumption even when the week contains fewer than forty hours. A weekly-only assumption can produce a different answer. In dated mode, daily overtime groups shifts by their starting work date, and weekly mode expects one seven-day workweek.
Select the single supported overtime method you intend to model. The form does not automatically combine every jurisdiction’s daily, weekly, consecutive-day or premium-pay rules.

links.label: Enter dated shifts and choose the overtime method

sections.title: Review rounding and breaks before comparing payroll totals
paragraphs: Dated mode rounds each clock punch independently when rounding is enabled; break durations remain unrounded. Rounding the start and finish can change a shift differently from rounding its final duration. Keep original records so the result can be reconciled.

A break entry reduces counted hours; it does not decide whether an employee is entitled to pay for that break. The estimate also excludes tax withholding, benefits and other payroll deductions unless modeled separately.

sections.title: Use the result as an auditable calculation
paragraphs: Compare the hours, rate and overtime classification with the underlying timesheet before relying on the estimated gross amount. The Time Card Calculator does not determine employment status, exemption, minimum wages or legal eligibility for overtime.
For a single interval, use Hours Calculator. For a net-pay planning estimate, use the applicable salary or take-home-pay tool with the correct country/year assumptions.

time-card-calculator.seoTitle: Time Card Calculator: Hours, Breaks & Overtime Pay

time-zone-calculator.description: Convert dates and times using named-zone daylight-saving rules or explicit fixed UTC offsets, with repeated-time handling.

faqs.question: Why did the destination date change?
faqs.answer: The offset difference moved the instant across midnight. Always read the destination date together with its time.

faqs.question: Is UTC−05:00 the same as America/New_York?
faqs.answer: Not for every date. A fixed offset stays constant; a named zone can apply seasonal and historical offset rules.

faqs.question: What does earlier or later occurrence mean?
faqs.answer: It selects between the two instants represented by a repeated local clock reading during a backward offset transition.

faqs.question: Why is a local time rejected?
faqs.answer: A clock jump can skip that reading entirely. Choose a valid time or verify the source record and zone.

faqs.question: Can I enter a half-hour or quarter-hour offset?
faqs.answer: Yes in fixed-offset mode using the signed hours:minutes format, such as +05:30 or +05:45.

faqs.question: Can the offset for a future date change?
faqs.answer: Yes. Authorities can change rules. Named-zone calculations depend on available time-zone data, so confirm important future schedules when rules are updated.

sections.title: Convert one instant, not just a number of hours
paragraphs: Enter the source date and local time, then choose a named source and destination zone. The calculator resolves the source clock reading to a UTC instant and formats that same instant in the destination. The destination date can be earlier or later than the source date.

A named zone such as America/New_York includes date-dependent rules. A fixed offset such as −05:00 specifies an offset only and does not switch seasonally. Use the mode matching the information you actually have.

sections.title: Worked fixed-offset example with a quarter-hour offset
paragraphs: At 12:00 on 9 October 2026 in UTC+05:45, subtract 5 hours 45 minutes to obtain 06:15 UTC. Moving to UTC−04:00 then subtracts another four hours, giving 02:15 on the same date. No daylight-saving inference is made in fixed-offset mode.

table.caption: One instant expressed at three fixed offsets

sections.title: Check the date when a conversion crosses midnight
paragraphs: For a source reading of 01:00 at UTC+09:00, the equivalent UTC time is 16:00 on the preceding calendar date. Comparing clock times without the date would lose that day change.
Offsets are not all whole hours. Keep the minutes in offsets such as +05:30 or +05:45, and do not treat +5.5 as an hours:minutes string.

sections.title: Resolve daylight-saving gaps and repeated times
paragraphs: When an offset jumps forward, some local clock readings do not exist; named-zone mode rejects those inputs. When clocks move backward, a local time can occur twice, and the earlier/later occurrence choice identifies which instant you intend.
This choice matters for elapsed durations. Two identically written local times can be an hour apart during a repeat. Compare the UTC instants when measuring the actual interval.

links.label: Compare dated endpoints after converting to UTC

sections.title: Use named zones carefully for future schedules
paragraphs: Time-zone rules can change by government decision. Conversion depends on the time-zone data available to the runtime, so a distant future appointment may need checking again after rules change. An abbreviation alone can also be ambiguous across regions.
Record the place or named zone along with a scheduled local time. Keep the resulting UTC instant when the task needs a single unambiguous event, rather than only a recurring local clock reading.

links.label: IANA time-zone database and rule updates

time-zone-calculator.seoTitle: Time Zone Converter: Named Zones & UTC Offsets

conversion-calculator.description: Convert length, area, volume, mass, speed, energy, data and temperature units, with US, imperial and binary distinctions made explicit.

faqs.question: Why is 1 m² not 100 cm²?
faqs.answer: Area uses two length dimensions. Because 1 m = 100 cm, 1 m² = 100² = 10,000 cm².

faqs.question: Are US and UK gallons interchangeable?
faqs.answer: No. A US gallon is approximately 3.785 L and an imperial gallon approximately 4.546 L. Select the exact type.

faqs.question: What is the difference between MB and MiB?
faqs.answer: MB uses a power of 1,000; MiB uses a power of 1,024. One MiB contains 1,048,576 bytes.

faqs.question: Can I convert kilograms directly to newtons?
faqs.answer: You also need gravitational acceleration. Use the Weight Calculator to calculate force from mass and gravity.

faqs.question: Can I use the Celsius converter for a temperature change?
faqs.answer: The reading conversion includes an offset. For differences, use only the scale factor: Δ°F = 1.8 × Δ°C.

faqs.question: Why does the answer have more decimal places than my input?
faqs.answer: The conversion can retain arithmetic precision, but the measurement uncertainty still comes from the original input.

sections.title: Start with the physical quantity, then select both units
paragraphs: Choose a category such as length, area, volume or temperature before entering the value. Units within a category describe the same quantity. Converting meters to feet changes the numerical scale; it does not turn a length into an area or a mass into a force.
Most conversions multiply by a fixed factor. Temperature readings also need an offset, so the same multiply-only shortcut cannot be used for Celsius and Fahrenheit.

sections.title: Worked conversions that expose common scaling mistakes
paragraphs: One meter is 100 centimeters, but a square meter is 100 × 100 = 10,000 square centimeters. A cubic meter contains 1,000 liters. Apply the power of the length conversion to match the quantity being converted.

table.caption: Check dimensions as well as numerical factors

sections.title: Distinguish US gallons, imperial gallons and liters
paragraphs: A US gallon is 3.785411784 L, whereas an imperial gallon is 4.54609 L. A bare gallon label is therefore incomplete. Select the specific gallon type from the unit menu, particularly when comparing fuel economy, tanks or product labels.
Similarly, a tonne is a metric mass unit. It should not silently replace a US short ton in a shipping or aggregate estimate. Choose the exact unit supported by the relevant calculator.

sections.title: Keep bits, bytes and binary prefixes separate
paragraphs: A byte contains eight bits. In the Data category, MB denotes a decimal megabyte and MiB denotes a binary mebibyte: 1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes and 1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes. The different labels can explain apparently inconsistent storage or transfer totals.
A data quantity is not a transfer rate. Use the Bandwidth Calculator when you need to combine a file size with a rate and estimate time.

sections.title: Avoid adding false precision to a measurement
paragraphs: Exact unit factors do not make an approximate input exact. If a measured length is known only to the nearest centimeter, a long decimal result in feet should not be treated as a more precise measurement. Keep sufficient digits during calculation and round to suit the original measurement.

The Temperature mode converts absolute readings and rejects values below absolute zero. A temperature difference follows a different rule: a change of 1 °C corresponds to a change of 1.8 °F, without adding 32.

conversion-calculator.seoTitle: Unit Converter: Length, Area, Volume & More

density-calculator.description: Find density from mass and volume, or solve for mass or volume using the labeled SI-unit relationship.

faqs.question: What is the density formula?
faqs.answer: Density equals mass divided by volume. For the basic fields, kilograms divided by cubic meters gives kg/m³.

faqs.question: How do I convert g/cm³ to kg/m³?
faqs.answer: Multiply by 1,000. Thus 2.7 g/cm³ equals 2,700 kg/m³.

faqs.question: Can the calculator find volume?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select the inverse mode and solve for volume using V = m/ρ.

faqs.question: Is density the same as weight?
faqs.answer: No. Density relates mass to volume; weight is a force that also depends on gravity.

faqs.question: Why might a supplier’s density differ from my measurement?
faqs.answer: The material state, moisture, temperature, compaction or measurement boundary may differ. Check that both values describe the same conditions.

sections.title: Density describes mass per unit volume
paragraphs: Density is ρ = m/V. In the basic mode, enter mass in kilograms and volume in cubic meters to obtain kilograms per cubic meter. The denominator must be a positive volume. Select the inverse mode when density and one other quantity are known.
A density value applies to a material or a sample under stated conditions. It does not by itself identify the substance, and the density of a loose bulk material can include spaces between particles.

sections.title: Worked example: convert the sample before dividing
paragraphs: A 0.54 kg sample occupying 0.0002 m³ has density 0.54/0.0002 = 2,700 kg/m³. The same volume is 200 cm³ and the same mass is 540 g, so the equivalent density is 2.7 g/cm³.
Entering 200 as a cubic-meter value would produce a result a million times too small. The unit printed beside each input is part of the calculation.

table.caption: One sample written in compatible unit systems

sections.title: Rearrange the equation to find mass or volume
paragraphs: With a density of 2,700 kg/m³, a 0.01 m³ portion has mass 2,700 × 0.01 = 27 kg. Conversely, 27 kg occupies 27/2,700 = 0.01 m³ under the same density assumption. These are algebraic rearrangements of one relationship.
If density or volume varies across the sample, one representative value may not describe every part. Add masses of separate portions when their densities differ.

links.label: Find mass or volume from density

sections.title: Distinguish density from weight and specific gravity
paragraphs: Mass density uses mass per volume. Weight density uses force per volume and depends on gravitational acceleration. Specific gravity is a ratio to a stated reference density and is dimensionless; it is not automatically the same numerical input as kg/m³.
When a specification gives g/mL, note that 1 g/mL = 1,000 kg/m³. Convert the supplied value before using the basic SI inputs.

sections.title: Keep measurement conditions with the result
paragraphs: Temperature, pressure, moisture and compaction can affect a measured density, depending on the material. Use the value appropriate to the sample and its state. A geometric volume estimate and a measured displaced volume may also describe different boundaries for a porous object.
Record how mass and volume were measured when comparing samples. Extra decimal places from division cannot correct an inaccurate volume measurement.

mass-calculator.description: Calculate mass from density and volume with independent measurement units. Select a result unit and keep mass distinct from gravitational weight.

faqs.question: How do I find mass from density?
faqs.answer: Multiply density by a compatible volume. A density of 800 kg/m³ and volume of 0.005 m³ give 4 kg.

faqs.question: Can I enter liters without converting to cubic meters?
faqs.answer: Yes in the multiple-unit mode. Choose L for the volume input and the matching density unit.

faqs.question: Does one liter always have a mass of one kilogram?
faqs.answer: No. Mass depends on the material’s density and conditions. One liter is a volume, not a fixed mass.

faqs.question: What if my material contains air spaces?
faqs.answer: Use an appropriate bulk density when those spaces are part of the measured volume.

faqs.question: Will this tell me how much force the load exerts?
faqs.answer: Not by mass alone. Use the Weight Calculator with the relevant gravitational acceleration to calculate force.

sections.title: Calculate mass from density and volume
paragraphs: The relation is m = ρV. Use the basic mode for density in kg/m³ and volume in m³, or select Density and volume in multiple units to convert each input independently. The output mass is determined by both the density assumption and the measured volume.
A container’s nominal capacity does not establish the mass of its contents. Two materials filling the same container can have very different masses.

sections.title: Worked example: a five-liter material sample
paragraphs: Suppose a material has density 800 kg/m³ and occupies 5 L. Five liters is 0.005 m³, so its mass is 800 × 0.005 = 4 kg. Enter those units directly in the multiple-unit mode or convert the volume before using the basic mode.

table.caption: Separate volume conversion from mass calculation

links.label: Use independent density and volume units

sections.title: Choose bulk density when the volume includes voids
paragraphs: For a loose material, the measured container volume can include spaces between particles. Use a bulk density describing that state when estimating the whole load. A solid-particle density applied to the same bulk volume can give a different and unsuitable mass estimate.

For several different materials, calculate each mass with its own density and volume, then add the masses. Do not multiply the combined volume by one material’s density unless that is an explicit approximation.

sections.title: Check whether the supplied quantity is mass or force
paragraphs: Kilograms, grams, pounds of mass and tonnes describe mass. Newtons and pounds-force describe force. Some density specifications use force-based units and therefore imply a gravity convention; read the selected unit carefully.
The resulting mass does not change merely because the object is moved to a place with different gravity. Its gravitational weight does change, as modeled by the Weight Calculator.

sections.title: Interpret precision and purchasing quantities separately
paragraphs: If the five-liter example actually contains 4.8–5.2 L, the density assumption gives 3.84–4.16 kg. A highly precise displayed number should not hide that measurement range.

Packaging increments, minimum delivery amounts and scale tolerances are separate from calculated mass. For construction materials, use the relevant material tool when you also need volume allowances or bags.

mass-calculator.seoTitle: Mass Calculator: Density, Volume & Unit Conversion

weight-calculator.description: Convert mass units or calculate gravitational weight from mass and an entered local acceleration, keeping mass and force distinct.

faqs.question: Is weight measured in kilograms or newtons?
faqs.answer: In physics, mass is measured in kilograms and weight force in newtons. Everyday scale readings are commonly labeled in kilograms.

faqs.question: What is the weight formula?
faqs.answer: W = m × g: multiply mass in kg by gravitational acceleration in m/s² to obtain newtons.

faqs.question: Why can the same mass have different weight?
faqs.answer: Weight force depends on gravity. The mass can remain the same while the gravitational acceleration changes.

faqs.question: How many kilograms are in one pound?
faqs.answer: One pound of mass equals exactly 0.45359237 kg.

faqs.question: Can this calculate an impact force?
faqs.answer: No. Impact calculations also depend on motion and the stopping process; mass times gravity alone does not describe them.

sections.title: Choose mass conversion or gravitational weight
paragraphs: Everyday language often calls a kilogram reading “weight,” but kilograms are a mass unit. Mass unit conversion changes between units such as kg, lb and g. The force calculation instead uses W = mg and reports newtons.
Select the task before entering numbers. Converting 70 kg into pounds does not require gravity; calculating the force on a 70 kg object does.

sections.title: Worked force example at the entered gravity
paragraphs: For mass 70 kg and acceleration 9.80665 m/s², weight force is 70 × 9.80665 = 686.4655 N. The gravity value is an explicit input, so the same mass can produce a different force under a different acceleration.
The table varies the mass while keeping this chosen gravity fixed. It illustrates the linear relationship, not a claim that gravity is identical at every location.

table.caption: Weight force at g = 9.80665 m/s²

sections.title: Convert pounds and kilograms with the correct meaning
paragraphs: One pound of mass is 0.45359237 kg. Thus 10 lb equals 4.5359237 kg. This mass conversion does not use the local gravitational acceleration. Pounds-force are a different unit and should not be entered as pounds of mass.
Keep a unit label on a result copied into an engineering equation. An unlabeled “150 pounds” can conceal whether the quantity is intended as mass or force.

sections.title: Know what a mass-times-gravity calculation excludes
paragraphs: The simple force result represents gravitational weight under the entered acceleration. It does not calculate impact force, acceleration loads, buoyancy or apparent scale readings in an accelerating system. Those situations require additional information.
For an object whose mass is not known but whose density and volume are available, calculate mass first and then use it here.

links.label: Find mass from density and volume

weight-calculator.seoTitle: Weight Calculator: Mass Conversion & Gravity Force

speed-calculator.description: Calculate speed, distance or travel time, including speed from independently selected distance units and an elapsed-duration input.

faqs.question: How do I calculate average speed?
faqs.answer: Divide total distance by total elapsed time. Use compatible units and decide whether the elapsed time includes stops.

faqs.question: How do I enter 2 hours 30 minutes?
faqs.answer: Enter 2.5 as decimal hours or 2:30:00 in the measured mode’s duration format.

faqs.question: How do I convert km/h to m/s?
faqs.answer: Divide by 3.6. For example, 60 km/h is approximately 16.6667 m/s.

faqs.question: Can I average 60 km/h and 30 km/h to get a journey speed?
faqs.answer: Only with the appropriate weighting. Equal-distance segments at those speeds average 40 km/h because the slower segment takes longer.

faqs.question: Does this estimate traffic delays?
faqs.answer: No. It calculates from entered distance and speed. Use a route-specific tool for driving-distance and route estimates.

faqs.question: Is pace the same as speed?
faqs.answer: They are reciprocal descriptions when units are handled correctly. Pace is time per distance; speed is distance per time.

sections.title: Use distance and elapsed time in compatible units
paragraphs: Average speed is distance divided by elapsed time. The basic mode uses kilometers and hours; the measured mode lets you choose distance, speed and duration units. It can solve for speed, distance or time, or convert an existing speed.
Decide whether elapsed time includes stops. The same journey can have a higher moving average than its door-to-door average. Neither result is the instantaneous speed at every point.

sections.title: Worked journey: 150 kilometers in two hours thirty minutes
paragraphs: Two hours thirty minutes is 2.5 hours. The average speed is 150/2.5 = 60 km/h. Dividing by 3.6 gives approximately 16.6667 m/s. In the measured mode, use 2:30:00 with the hours:minutes:seconds format or 2.5 with decimal hours.

table.caption: Three rearrangements of the journey calculation

links.label: Choose measurement units and duration format

sections.title: Do not average unequal journey segments blindly
paragraphs: For two equal distances of 60 km, traveling one at 60 km/h takes one hour and the other at 30 km/h takes two hours. The combined average is 120 km/3 h = 40 km/h, not the arithmetic mean of 45 km/h.
Add the total distance and total time before dividing. A direct average of speeds is appropriate only under the weighting that matches the time spent at each speed.

sections.title: Separate speed, pace and velocity
paragraphs: Pace expresses time per unit distance, such as minutes per kilometer; speed expresses distance per time. A speed of 12 km/h corresponds to 60/12 = 5 minutes per kilometer. Use Pace Calculator for common running pace formats.
Velocity also includes direction. This tool does not reconstruct a path, displacement vector or acceleration profile from one distance and one elapsed time.

sections.title: Treat travel-time results as constant-average estimates
paragraphs: Time = distance/speed assumes the entered speed represents the whole interval. Traffic, turns, stops and terrain can make a real trip differ. The calculation does not retrieve a road route or live traffic.
A zero speed cannot produce a finite travel time for a positive distance. Check for empty values, zero denominators and hours-versus-minutes errors before interpreting an unexpected result.

speed-calculator.seoTitle: Speed Calculator: Distance, Time & Average Speed

molarity-calculator.description: Calculate molarity, solute mass or solution volume, and convert concentration units with explicit density for mass-fraction ppm or ppb.

faqs.question: What is the molarity formula from grams?
faqs.answer: Divide solute mass by molar mass to obtain moles, then divide by final solution volume in liters.

faqs.question: Do I enter solvent volume or solution volume?
faqs.answer: Enter the final solution volume. The solvent volume before adding solute may differ from the final volume.

faqs.question: How many mM are in 0.1 M?
faqs.answer: 0.1 M equals 100 mM because one mole is 1,000 millimoles.

faqs.question: Can I find grams needed for a solution?
faqs.answer: Yes. Required mass uses m = concentration × molar mass × final volume with compatible units.

faqs.question: Is ppm always the same as mg/L?
faqs.answer: No. A mass-fraction ppm value requires density to convert to mass per volume. The unit-aware mode requires that density where needed.

faqs.question: Can I use an anhydrous molar mass for a hydrate?
faqs.answer: No. Include the hydrate’s water and other formula components so the molar mass matches the weighed substance.

sections.title: Use moles of solute and the final solution volume
paragraphs: Molarity is amount of solute divided by final solution volume: c = n/V. With solute mass m and molar mass M, n = m/M, so c = m/(MV). The basic mode uses grams, grams per mole and liters to produce mol/L.
Enter the final solution volume, not the volume of solvent before dissolving. The calculation assumes the entered mass refers to the stated solute and molar mass.

sections.title: Worked example: 5.844 grams at 58.44 grams per mole
paragraphs: Using an illustrative molar mass of 58.44 g/mol, 5.844 g represents 0.100 mol. In a final volume of 1.000 L, the concentration is 0.100 mol/L, or 100 mM. Halving the final volume while keeping the same solute amount doubles the concentration.

table.caption: Same solute amount, different final volumes

sections.title: Find the mass required for a chosen concentration
paragraphs: Rearrange the equation to m = cMV. At 0.100 mol/L, molar mass 58.44 g/mol and final volume 0.250 L, the required pure-solute mass is 1.461 g. Required mass mode performs this arithmetic directly.

Purity, hydration state and the correct chemical species matter. For example, a hydrate has a different molar mass from its anhydrous form. This calculator does not infer those details from a generic compound name.

links.label: Check a chemical formula’s molar mass

sections.title: Do not equate molarity, mass concentration and ppm automatically
paragraphs: Molar concentration and mass concentration are linked by molar mass. For the stated 58.44 g/mol example, 0.1 mol/L corresponds to 5.844 g/L. A concentration of 1 M is not a universal number of grams per liter.

Mass-fraction ppm and ppb additionally need solution density when converting to a volume-based concentration. The unit-aware mode asks for density instead of assuming every solution has the density of water.

sections.title: Keep the chemical and measurement assumptions explicit
paragraphs: Use positive, compatible volume and molar-mass inputs. A rounded molecular mass, uncertain purity or inaccurate final volume affects the resulting concentration even when the arithmetic is exact.

The result is a composition calculation. It is not a laboratory procedure, a stability prediction or a medication-dosing instruction. Follow the appropriate validated protocol for an actual preparation.

molecular-weight-calculator.description: Calculate molar mass and an element-by-element mass breakdown from a supported chemical formula and versioned atomic-mass data.

faqs.question: Why does capitalization matter?
faqs.answer: Element symbols are case-sensitive. Co and CO describe different elemental compositions.

faqs.question: Can I enter parentheses?
faqs.answer: Yes. A subscript after parentheses or square brackets multiplies the entire enclosed group.

faqs.question: Does the tool support hydrates?
faqs.answer: Yes, supported hydrate notation includes a dot separator and a coefficient such as CuSO4·5H2O. Check the resulting atom counts.

faqs.question: Why does my textbook give a slightly different molar mass?
faqs.answer: Tables can use different rounding or reference atomic weights. Compare the per-element contributions and the precision required for your task.

faqs.question: Can I calculate an isotope-labeled ion?
faqs.answer: Not with this parser’s current input scope. It does not support isotopic labels or charged-species notation.

faqs.question: Does it balance a chemical equation?
faqs.answer: No. It sums the atoms in the entered formula and reports their mass contribution.

sections.title: Enter an exact chemical formula, including element capitalization
paragraphs: The calculator adds each element’s stored atomic mass multiplied by its atom count. Element symbols are case-sensitive: Co denotes cobalt, whereas CO denotes carbon and oxygen. Use the formula rather than a common compound name.
Parentheses and square brackets group atoms, and a number following a group multiplies every atom inside it. Hydrate notation can include a middle dot and a coefficient for the water portion.

sections.title: Worked example: expand Ca(OH)2 before adding masses
paragraphs: Ca(OH)2 contains one calcium atom, two oxygen atoms and two hydrogen atoms. Using the calculator’s stored values, the contributions are 40.08 + 2 × 15.999 + 2 × 1.008 = 74.094 g/mol.
The element breakdown lets you check the parsed counts before using the total. A missing closing bracket or incorrect subscript can change the chemical formula itself, not merely the formatting.

table.caption: Atom-by-atom contribution for calcium hydroxide

sections.title: Check hydrates and leading coefficients carefully
paragraphs: A formula such as CuSO4·5H2O includes five water units: ten hydrogen atoms and five additional oxygen atoms. Omitting the hydrate portion gives the mass of a different formula. Review the atom-count table after entering grouped or hydrated formulas.

The parser does not balance chemical reactions or infer which compound a name refers to. Enter one supported formula and use the separate concentration tool when converting its molar mass into grams or molarity.

links.label: Use molar mass in a solution calculation

sections.title: Distinguish average atomic weights from isotope-specific masses
paragraphs: This tool uses its stored periodic-table dataset rather than selecting individual isotope masses. Natural isotopic composition and the rounding of reference tables can make published totals differ slightly. Isotopic labels and charged-species notation are outside this parser’s supported input scope.
Check whether your task needs an average formula mass, an isotope-specific mass or a value rounded for a teaching exercise. A displayed decimal total is not a claim of isotope-level precision.

links.label: CIAAW: standard atomic weights and their scope

sections.title: Use the total with the correct unit relationship
paragraphs: The displayed molar mass is in grams per mole. If a formula has molar mass 74.094 g/mol, 0.25 mol has mass 18.5235 g under the same stored mass convention. Divide grams by g/mol to convert a sample mass back into moles.

Molecular mass and molar mass have closely related numerical values under the stated atomic-mass convention, but their units and the amount of material being described differ. Keep the units when transferring a result into another formula.

molecular-weight-calculator.seoTitle: Molecular Weight Calculator: Formula & Molar Mass

gdp-calculator.description: Calculate expenditure-based GDP or reconcile entered income components, capital consumption and statistical discrepancy to a domestic total.

faqs.question: What is the GDP expenditure formula?
faqs.answer: GDP = C + I + G + X − M, with consumption, investment, government expenditure, exports and imports measured consistently.

faqs.question: Why are imports subtracted?
faqs.answer: Imported production may already be inside the spending components. Subtracting imports keeps the expenditure total focused on domestic production.

faqs.question: Can I mix annual and quarterly figures?
faqs.answer: No. Use the same accounting period and check whether a published quarterly series has been annualized.

faqs.question: Does this calculate real GDP automatically?
faqs.answer: No. It adds the entered components. It does not apply a price deflator or retrieve inflation-adjusted national accounts.

faqs.question: Does investment mean stock-market purchases?
faqs.answer: Not generally in this identity. Use the investment definition in the relevant national accounts, rather than an individual portfolio’s transactions.

faqs.question: Can the income and expenditure results differ?
faqs.answer: Measured accounts can include a statistical discrepancy. Use consistent source definitions and the appropriate reconciliation rather than silently forcing equality.

sections.title: Keep the national-accounting components compatible
paragraphs: The expenditure identity is GDP = consumption + investment + government expenditure + exports − imports. Enter every component for the same economy, period, currency and scale. If one series is in billions and another in millions, the resulting sum is not meaningful.

The investment component uses national-accounts definitions, not an individual investor’s purchases of existing shares. Use components prepared on a consistent accounting basis rather than mixing similarly named household-budget categories.

sections.title: Worked expenditure example with negative net exports
paragraphs: With consumption 14,000, investment 4,000, government expenditure 4,000, exports 3,000 and imports 3,500, net exports equal −500. GDP is therefore 14,000 + 4,000 + 4,000 − 500 = 21,500 in the chosen common scale.
If all inputs are billions of one currency for the same year, the output is 21,500 billion of that currency for that year. The calculator does not retrieve or verify a country’s latest statistics.

table.caption: Illustrative expenditure components

sections.title: Why imports are subtracted without treating them as lost output
paragraphs: Imports can already be included in consumption, investment or government spending. The subtraction removes foreign production from the measure of domestic production. It does not mean an imported purchase is necessarily harmful or that exports and imports alone determine national welfare.

Avoid counting intermediate transactions repeatedly. National-accounting aggregates are designed to measure production consistently; simply adding every observed business receipt is not the same calculation.

sections.title: Use the income method with the correct net and gross basis
paragraphs: Income-based national accounts offers detailed and aggregate income components plus the stated adjustments. Keep domestic versus national income and net versus gross values distinct. Capital consumption and a statistical discrepancy are not arbitrary balancing entries to insert without a source.

Select the basis matching the supplied accounts, and avoid entering both a detailed component and an aggregate that already includes it. Expenditure and income estimates can differ in measured data even though the accounting concepts are linked.

sections.title: Interpret nominal GDP separately from growth and living standards
paragraphs: This arithmetic does not remove price changes, convert currencies using purchasing-power parity or divide by population. A larger nominal number can reflect prices, exchange-rate conventions, population or production rather than one uniquely defined improvement.

For comparisons over time, use consistent published real or nominal series as appropriate. For comparisons across economies, specify the currency conversion, price basis and period before interpreting the result.

gpa-calculator.description: Calculate semester and cumulative GPA using course grades, credit hours, and your institution’s grading scale.
gpa-calculator.seoTitle: College GPA Calculator: Semester & Cumulative GPA

sections.title: How GPA is calculated from grades and credit hours
paragraphs: GPA = total quality points ÷ total graded credits. For each included course, quality points equal its grade-point value multiplied by its credits. A 4-credit course therefore affects GPA more than a 2-credit course with the same grade-point change.

Choose Courses & semester GPA, select Letter grades, Grade points or Percentages, and enter each course once. Use the Semester field to group the results. Open Grade scale to check the editable mappings and maximum against your school’s rules before calculating; the starting scale is an example, not a universal conversion.

table.caption: A nine-credit semester using A = 4, B = 3 and C = 2

links.label: Enter course grades and credit hours

sections.title: Read the semester GPA and cumulative GPA as different totals
paragraphs: The example semester has 29 quality points over 9 graded credits, so its GPA is 29 ÷ 9 = 3.2222, or about 3.22. The unweighted average of A, B and C would be 3.00, because it would ignore the unequal credits.

Now suppose your previous cumulative GPA is 2.80 over 30 graded credits. Those earlier courses represent 2.80 × 30 = 84 quality points. Combining the records gives (84 + 29) ÷ (30 + 9) = 113 ÷ 39 = 2.8974, or about 2.90. Averaging 2.80 and 3.22 directly would give the two records equal weight even though one contains over three times as many credits.

Enter Previous cumulative GPA 2.8 and Previous graded credits 30 for this example. Do not also list those same prior courses in the course rows. If your transcript supplies more precision than its displayed GPA, use the most precise approved figure available when recreating the result.

table.caption: Combine records through quality points and graded credits

sections.title: Check the 4.0 scale, plus/minus grades and percentage cutoffs
paragraphs: The table below records Finflo’s starting letter scale. Open Grade scale to edit it in the form. For example, a school may use B+ = 3.33 instead of 3.3, or assign a different value to A+. Change both the mapping and Maximum grade points when the official scale requires it; changing the maximum alone does not rewrite the letter values.

Percentage grades also require a specified conversion table. Select Percentages, open Grade scale and edit the minimum-percentage cutoffs to match your institution. In Finflo’s starting percentage example, 85% maps to 3 grade points because it reaches the 80% cutoff but not 90%. Dividing 85 by 25 would produce 3.4 and would not follow that example table. Neither rule is a universal conversion.

For a 10-point cumulative GPA (CGPA), select Grade points and set Maximum grade points to 10 under Grade scale. Enter the official grade points rather than rescaling percentages yourself. Four credits at 9 points, three at 8 and two at 7 produce 74 quality points over 9 credits: approximately 8.22. Previous GPA and new courses must use the same scale.

table.caption: Editable starting letter scale; use your institution’s actual values
headers: Grade points in the starting example

links.label: University of Illinois: an institution-specific grade-point scale

sections.title: Distinguish excluded courses from a zero-grade-point F
paragraphs: An excluded course contributes neither quality points nor graded credits. A GPA-bearing F contributes zero quality points but still adds its graded credits. Adding a 3-credit excluded P to the nine-credit example leaves 29 ÷ 9 ≈ 3.22. If that same 3-credit course instead carries an included F, the result becomes 29 ÷ 12 ≈ 2.42.

Use Include in GPA = No for a row your institution excludes, or define an excluded grade symbol in the editable letter scale. The starting P and NP exclusions are example settings, not a ruling about every pass/fail system. Check the treatment of withdrawals, incompletes, transfer work and failed pass/fail courses before entering them.

sections.title: Model weighted high-school or honors GPA with the actual grade points
paragraphs: Credit weighting and honors weighting are separate. Credits determine how strongly a course counts in the average; an honors or AP policy may also change the grade-point value assigned to that course. Finflo does not automatically add a bonus based on the course name.

If your school assigns 5 points to an A in one advanced course and 4 points to an A in a regular course, choose Grade points, open Grade scale and set Maximum grade points to at least 5. An illustrative 3-credit course at 5 points and a 4-credit course at 4 points produce (3 × 5 + 4 × 4) ÷ 7 = 4.4286. Enter the already adjusted points from the applicable policy; do not add an honors bonus twice.

sections.title: Handle repeated courses and transcript rounding explicitly
paragraphs: The calculator does not decide which attempt replaces a repeated course or which transfer courses belong in your GPA. Include the attempts required by your institution’s policy. If a previous cumulative total contains an attempt that is now removed, use the corrected prior GPA and graded credits; excluding a newly entered row does not remove points already inside the previous total.

A displayed estimate may differ slightly from an official transcript because of the scale, exclusions, stored precision or final reporting rule. For example, the University of Illinois reports GPA to two decimal places by truncation. Finflo’s displayed numerical rounding is not a substitute for that institution’s reporting procedure. Keep the underlying quality-point calculation when checking a boundary.

links.label: University of Illinois: quality points, GPA hours and transcript reporting
Stanford: examples of grade symbols and repeated-course notation

sections.title: Estimate the GPA needed in future courses
paragraphs: To raise a 2.80 cumulative GPA over 30 graded credits to 3.00 after another 15 graded credits, the future courses must average [3.00 × 45 − 2.80 × 30] ÷ 15 = 3.40. The required value depends on both the target and the number of future graded credits.

Use the GPA Goal Calculator for that calculation and its alternative scenarios. Improving a future semester affects an established cumulative GPA less when many credits are already completed. The planner compares the required future GPA with your selected maximum rather than assuming every target is reachable.

links.label: Calculate the future GPA needed for your target
Calculate a course percentage before converting it to a grade

faqs.question: How do I calculate GPA with credit hours?
faqs.answer: Multiply each included course’s grade points by its credits, add those quality points, and divide by the included credits. The example 4-credit A, 3-credit B and 2-credit C gives 29 quality points over 9 credits: approximately 3.22 on the stated scale.

faqs.question: What is the difference between semester GPA and cumulative GPA?
faqs.answer: Semester GPA covers the courses grouped into that semester. Cumulative GPA combines their quality points and graded credits with the earlier record. Unequal-credit semesters must not be averaged as if they had equal weight.

faqs.question: Does an A+ count as 4.0 or 4.3?
faqs.answer: That depends on the institution. Finflo’s starting A+ value is 4.0. Open Grade scale to edit the letter table. If your school uses 4.3, update the A+ row and set Maximum grade points to at least 4.3.

faqs.question: Can I convert a percentage directly into GPA?
faqs.answer: Only after specifying the conversion scale. Choose Percentages, open Grade scale and edit the cutoffs to the applicable school policy. A single formula such as percentage divided by 25 is not a universal GPA conversion.

faqs.question: Can I calculate CGPA on a 10-point scale?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose Grade points, open Grade scale and set Maximum grade points to 10. Enter the institution’s official points and GPA-bearing credits, using the same scale for previous GPA. This computes the entered credit-weighted average; it does not certify equivalence between different institutions or convert an arbitrary percentage into CGPA.

faqs.question: Do pass/fail, withdrawals or incompletes count toward GPA?
faqs.answer: Use your institution’s rules. Set Include in GPA to No for a course that is excluded, or define an excluded grade symbol in the letter scale. An included F is different: it adds graded credits with zero quality points.

faqs.question: Can this calculate weighted high-school GPA?
faqs.answer: Yes, when you enter the grade-point values and credits specified by your school. Use Grade points for course-specific honors or AP values and open Grade scale to set an adequate maximum. The calculator does not identify course difficulty or add bonuses automatically.

faqs.question: Can I include my previous GPA without entering every past course?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enter Previous cumulative GPA and Previous graded credits, then add only courses not already included in that record. Correct the prior totals first if a repeat or exclusion changes the historical GPA.

faqs.question: Why does the result differ from my transcript?
faqs.answer: Check plus/minus values, included credits, repeated-course treatment, transfer work and reporting precision. Institutions can round or truncate differently. Your registrar’s official record determines the reported GPA.

faqs.question: How can I find the grades needed to raise my GPA?
faqs.answer: Open the GPA Goal Calculator with your current GPA, completed graded credits, target GPA and future graded credits. It calculates the required future average and shows whether it exceeds the selected scale maximum.

grade-calculator.description: Calculate weighted or points-based grades, exclude ungraded work, and compare what-if scores.

sections.title: How to calculate your grade from the course rules
paragraphs: A weighted grade is the sum of each score multiplied by its weight, divided by the sum of the included weights. Use percentages consistently: a score of 88% in a category worth 20% contributes 88 × 0.20 = 17.6 percentage points toward the whole course. A course that adds raw points instead uses 100 × total points earned ÷ total points possible.

Start with your syllabus and gradebook. Choose Category weights & what-if grades for categories such as homework and exams; use each category’s current average once.
