Separately verified deductions or credits need their own individual and joint amounts.

Likewise, the composed calculation keeps each person’s Social Security/self-employment wage cap separate while evaluating joint income thresholds where applicable. Unsupported items, community-property allocation and a joint-versus-married-filing-separately analysis require a different review. Use this result as a scenario comparison, not as a recommendation about marriage or filing status.

links.label: Inspect the underlying federal tax worksheets
Compare paycheck withholding after a status change

estate-tax-calculator.description: Estimate a 2026 federal estate-tax scenario from asset and deduction lines, adjusted gifts, exclusion and entered credit assumptions.

faqs.question: Do both estate modes use only a flat 40% rate?
faqs.answer: No. The legacy approximation uses the top rate above its entered exclusion. The detailed assets-and-gifts mode uses the graduated tentative-tax schedule and applicable exclusion credit.

faqs.question: Can I enter a deceased spouse’s unused exclusion?
faqs.answer: The detailed mode accepts a valid elected DSUE amount as an assumption. It does not determine portability eligibility or make the required election.

faqs.question: Are state inheritance taxes and all gift adjustments included?
faqs.answer: State and generation-skipping taxes are excluded. Adjusted taxable gifts, gift tax payable, deductions and other credits must be supplied after separate verification.

faqs.question: Is the $15 million exclusion a $15 million tax credit?
faqs.answer: No. The exclusion is a transfer amount. Under the 2026 unified rate schedule its corresponding basic tax credit is $5,945,800.

faqs.question: Does a zero estate-tax result mean no federal estate return is needed?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Filing requirements and a portability election can apply independently of the final tax due. Review the Form 706 rules for the actual estate.

faqs.question: Should gifts already made be deducted from estate assets again?
faqs.answer: Do not subtract the same property twice. Current estate assets and adjusted taxable gifts are separate inputs in the detailed cumulative calculation, using their separately verified tax treatment.

faqs.question: Does the estate worksheet estimate tax for every country or every death year?
faqs.answer: No. The detailed mode is a 2026 US citizen/resident federal scenario. Other jurisdictions, years and nonresident rules require the applicable parameters and method.

sections.title: Understanding a modeled taxable estate
paragraphs: The estate worksheet starts from the entered assets, adjustments, gifts, and supported credits. Keep estate value separate from the amount potentially subject to tax under the selected federal assumptions. The result is a planning estimate for the stated year and scope. It does not determine asset ownership, valuation disputes, state estate or inheritance taxes, or the effect of an unmodeled trust arrangement.

sections.title: Build the taxable estate from verified asset and deduction amounts
paragraphs: Use the detailed 2026 estate assets, gifts & credits mode to list included estate asset categories and separately established allowable deductions. The tool totals each list and subtracts deductions from gross estate. A balance-sheet value, a probate asset list and a federal gross estate are not automatically identical.

Use values and ownership interests appropriate to the applicable estate-tax rules. Do not subtract a debt from an asset value and then enter the same debt again as a deduction. The calculator performs arithmetic on the supplied categories; it does not establish whether insurance proceeds, a trust interest, jointly owned property or a claimed deduction belongs in the return.

links.label: IRS: estate-tax scope and asset inclusion

sections.title: Worked example: an $18 million gross estate in 2026
paragraphs: Assume $18 million of included assets, $1 million of allowable deductions, no adjusted taxable gifts, no gift-tax adjustment, no DSUE and no other credits. Taxable estate is $17 million. The graduated schedule produces tentative tax of $6,745,800, and the credit corresponding to the $15 million basic exclusion is $5,945,800. The modeled federal estate tax is $800,000.

The simple approximation gives the same answer here: ($17 million − $15 million) × 40%. This agreement depends on the clean high-value example; it does not make gifts, portability or credit adjustments interchangeable with a single exclusion subtraction.

table.caption: 2026 detailed estate example without gifts or portability

links.label: IRS Form 706: unified rate schedule and 2026 credit

sections.title: Keep an exclusion amount separate from its tax credit
paragraphs: The 2026 basic exclusion for this US citizen/resident model is $15 million. In the detailed calculation, an exclusion is converted into an applicable tax credit under the graduated rate schedule. The $15 million exclusion and its $5,945,800 credit are different quantities; neither is entered as an ordinary asset deduction.

A valid elected deceased-spouse unused exclusion, or DSUE, increases the exclusion input in the detailed mode. If the example has a separately verified $1 million DSUE amount, available exclusion becomes $16 million, its credit becomes $6,345,800 and modeled tax falls to $400,000. Entering an assumed second full exclusion merely because the decedent was married would not establish portability.

sections.title: Treat prior gifts and gift-tax adjustments as separate inputs
paragraphs: Adjusted taxable gifts affect the cumulative transfer-tax calculation and are not the same as every dollar given away during life. The detailed mode adds the entered adjusted taxable gifts to taxable estate, applies the graduated schedule, and then subtracts the entered gift-tax adjustment and applicable credits.

Use the adjusted gift amounts and tax payable determined under the relevant Form 706 rules. Do not enter the total of all gift-tax returns or tax payments without checking the required reconciliation. The legacy approximation only reduces its entered exclusion by the entered gifts and omits these detailed interactions.

sections.title: A zero estimate does not resolve filing or state-tax obligations
paragraphs: A federal estate-tax estimate can be zero while a return is still required or filed to elect portability. Filing thresholds and elections are separate questions from the final tax arithmetic. The IRS estate-tax instructions address those requirements and the records supporting them.

This page covers the stated 2026 US citizen/resident scenario. It does not calculate state estate or inheritance tax, generation-skipping transfer tax, nonresident noncitizen rules or an unentered trust arrangement. Verify valuations, elections and special situations with the relevant instructions and an estate-tax professional before relying on a plan.

links.label: IRS: estate filing and portability questions

rental-property-calculator.description: Estimate rental cash flow and returns, or model a holding period with growing expenses, mortgage payoff and sale proceeds.

faqs.question: Should mortgage payments be included in operating expenses?
faqs.answer: No. Operating expenses exclude debt service and depreciation. The model deducts mortgage payments separately when calculating cash flow.

faqs.question: How does a sale affect holding-period return?
faqs.answer: Final cash flow includes the sale proceeds after selling costs and remaining mortgage debt. It is counted once in the investor-return stream.

faqs.question: Why can cap rate be positive while cash flow is negative?
faqs.answer: Cap rate excludes debt service. Loan payments can exceed the income left after operating expenses.

faqs.question: Does cash-on-cash return include appreciation?
faqs.answer: The first-year measure uses cash flow relative to initial cash; it does not include an unrealized increase in property value.

faqs.question: Does the first-year result include a future sale?
faqs.answer: No. Use the holding-period method to include an assumed sale value, selling costs and remaining loan balance.

sections.title: Keep operating performance separate from financing
paragraphs: The first-year method reduces scheduled rent by the vacancy assumption, subtracts operating expenses to find net operating income, then subtracts loan payments to find cash flow. Enter debt service only through the loan fields; including it again in operating expenses would understate both NOI and cash flow.

sections.title: Worked example: a financed 200,000 property
paragraphs: With a 25% down payment, 5,000 closing costs, 1,600 monthly rent, 5% vacancy and 400 monthly operating expenses, NOI is 1,120 per month or 13,440 per year. Financing the remaining 150,000 at an assumed 6% over 30 years costs about 899.33 monthly, leaving 220.67 of monthly cash flow.

table.caption: Different return measures use different bases
rows: Monthly cash flow after debt service

sections.title: Cap rate and cash-on-cash return answer different questions
paragraphs: Cap rate compares NOI with purchase price before financing. Cash-on-cash return compares annual cash flow after debt service with the initial cash invested. Neither measure alone includes the full effect of appreciation, principal repayment, sale costs and investment duration.

sections.title: Use the holding-period method for growth and an eventual sale
paragraphs: The extended method adds repairs, expense lines, management charges, rent growth, a sale-price assumption and selling costs. Avoid double-counting management or other charges already entered separately. Vacancy, repairs, rent and resale value are assumptions, so compare weaker operating conditions as well as the central scenario.

sections.title: Comparing rental cash flow with sale proceeds
paragraphs: Rental income, operating costs, financing, and eventual sale proceeds affect different parts of an investment's return. Review ongoing cash flow separately from the holding-period result. An attractive sale assumption can hide weak annual cash flow, while a positive monthly figure may omit costs not entered. Compare scenarios using consistent vacancy, expense, financing, and holding-period assumptions.

rental-property-calculator.seoTitle: Rental Property Calculator: Cash Flow, Cap Rate & Returns

rent-vs-buy-calculator.description: Compare renting and buying through housing cash flows, refundable deposits, mortgage equity and a common investment-return assumption.

faqs.question: How does the detailed mode treat a refundable deposit?
faqs.answer: It records the deposit as an upfront renter outflow and the selected refund at exit. A full refund removes its nominal cost but can still have a present-value opportunity cost.

faqs.question: Is mortgage principal counted as an expense twice?
faqs.answer: No. The detailed mode includes payments in cash outflows and subtracts remaining loan debt from sale proceeds to calculate equity at exit.

faqs.question: What does the terminal buying advantage measure?
faqs.answer: In the detailed mode it grows the same present-value cost difference to the comparison end date. It is not an additional benefit to add to that difference.

faqs.question: Does the model assume renters invest money saved?
faqs.answer: Yes. It tracks upfront cash not used to buy and invests modeled ongoing cost differences under the entered return assumption.

faqs.question: Are all mortgage payments treated as lost money?
faqs.answer: No. Principal repayment reduces the remaining loan and contributes to equity.

faqs.question: Why does the result change when I shorten the stay?
faqs.answer: Buying and selling costs have fewer years over which to be offset by other financial differences.

faqs.question: Does the comparison automatically calculate mortgage tax deductions?
faqs.answer: No. The detailed method uses an explicitly entered tax-benefit assumption when selected; it does not establish deduction eligibility.

sections.title: Compare financial positions at the same future date
paragraphs: Buying uses an upfront down payment and closing costs, creates mortgage debt and may build equity. Renting leaves that initial cash available to invest. The model also invests the difference in ongoing costs for whichever side is cheaper, so compare the ending positions rather than treating every mortgage payment as an expense or every rent payment as the entire comparison.

sections.title: Worked example: a five-year holding period with no price growth
paragraphs: For a 200,000 home, 20% down, 2% buying costs, a 30-year mortgage at 6%, 300 monthly ownership costs and 5% selling costs, compare rent of 1,000 per month. With no rent growth, home appreciation or investment return, the five-year buyer position is about 41,113.03 and the renter position about 59,556.85.

table.caption: Illustration with zero growth assumptions
rows: Renter initial cash plus monthly savings

sections.title: The holding period can change the result
paragraphs: Purchase and sale costs are concentrated around moving dates, while principal repayment and any appreciation accumulate over time. Recalculate for the period you actually expect to stay. A small change in appreciation, rent growth or the return on savings can reverse a close comparison.

sections.title: Use detailed cost streams for a fuller household comparison
paragraphs: The detailed method separates ownership expense growth, renter insurance, deposits and an optional entered tax benefit. A refundable security deposit is tied-up cash rather than automatically a permanent expense. Nonfinancial factors such as flexibility, maintenance responsibility and housing stability remain outside the money calculation.

links.label: Estimate a rent budget from income

sections.title: Making a rent-or-buy comparison over one horizon
paragraphs: A rent-versus-buy result depends on how long you stay and what happens to housing costs, property value, and alternative savings. Compare both paths over the same horizon and review the treatment of deposits and ending equity. A refundable deposit is different from an expense. The model is especially sensitive to long-term assumptions, so test several scenarios before relying on a single break-even point.

rent-vs-buy-calculator.seoTitle: Rent vs Buy Calculator: Housing Costs & Ending Equity

currency-calculator.description: Convert currencies using an entered exchange rate, dated reference rates, or supported spot quotes. Check source dates and allow for provider fees and spreads.

faqs.question: Are ECB reference rates live transaction quotes?
faqs.answer: No. They are dated informational reference rates. Banks and payment providers may use different rates, spreads, fees or settlement times.

faqs.question: Are my amount and currency choices sent to the rate provider?
faqs.answer: No. The site fetches a generic reference-rate feed; your selected currencies and amount are used for conversion in the browser.

faqs.question: What does target currency per source unit mean?
faqs.answer: It is the amount of the destination currency bought by one unit of the starting currency, such as 0.90 EUR for 1 USD.

faqs.question: How do I reverse an exchange rate?
faqs.answer: Take its reciprocal. If one source unit buys r target units, one target unit buys 1/r source units before costs.

faqs.question: Why can the two currencies show different quote dates?
faqs.answer: The global method retains observations from its available sources, which may update on different schedules. Check both dates and provider details.

sections.title: Read the direction of the exchange rate first
paragraphs: The manual method expects units of the target currency for one unit of the source currency. Multiply the source amount by that rate. The ECB and global reference methods retrieve available reference observations and display their dates; they do not promise the exact price a bank or exchange provider will offer.

sections.title: Worked example: convert with a supplied rate
paragraphs: At an illustrative rate of 1 USD = 0.90 EUR, 500 USD converts to 450 EUR. To reverse the conversion under the same hypothetical no-fee rate, use 1/0.90 = 1.111111 USD per EUR. Reusing 0.90 in the reverse direction would be incorrect.

table.caption: Keep currency units attached to the rate

sections.title: Reference date and retrieval time are different
paragraphs: An observation date identifies the source rate; retrieval time records when the snapshot was obtained. A weekend or holiday can leave the latest published reference unchanged. Global source and target observations may have different dates, and the provider table exposes source details rather than implying every instrument was quoted simultaneously.

sections.title: Compare the final amount after provider costs
paragraphs: A bank’s spread, fixed charge, conversion fee or transfer fee can change the amount received. The manual rate can be used with a provider’s quoted exchange rate, but a separate fee must also be allowed for when comparing offers. Reference prices for currencies, metals or Bitcoin are informational snapshots rather than executable transaction prices.

links.label: Estimate a percentage and fixed payment fee

sections.title: Reading an exchange-rate result
paragraphs: Select the conversion mode according to whether you want an entered rate, a dated reference rate, or a supported spot quote. Check the source and timestamp shown with the result. A reference conversion is not a promise that a bank or payment provider will offer that amount. Fees, spreads, settlement timing, and unsupported dates can affect an actual exchange.

bmi-calculator.description: Calculate adult BMI or CDC BMI-for-age percentiles for ages 2 to under 20, with the screening limits of each method explained.

faqs.question: How do I calculate BMI manually?
faqs.answer: Divide kilograms by height in meters squared. At 70 kg and 1.75 m, BMI is 70 ÷ 1.75² = 22.8571, usually displayed as 22.86.

faqs.question: Do I enter feet or inches in US mode?
faqs.answer: Enter total inches. A height of 5 feet 9 inches is 69 inches. Enter weight in pounds when US units are selected.

faqs.question: Does a BMI percentile tell me body-fat percentage?
faqs.answer: No. A percentile compares BMI with a reference population of the same age and sex; it does not measure the share of the body made up of fat.

faqs.question: Can the adult mode be used for a teenager?
faqs.answer: Use Child & teen BMI-for-age for ages 2 to under 20. Finflo’s adult mode starts at age 20.

faqs.question: Why can a category look inconsistent with a rounded BMI?
faqs.answer: The category uses the unrounded value. Numbers close to 18.5, 25 or 30 can display at a boundary after rounding.

faqs.question: Does BMI diagnose a health condition?
faqs.answer: No. Interpretation can require body composition, medical history, growth patterns and other measurements beyond height and weight.

sections.title: Choose adult BMI or child BMI-for-age before entering measurements
paragraphs: Adult BMI divides weight in kilograms by height in meters squared. Choose Adult BMI for ages 20 and over. The Child & teen BMI-for-age mode uses age in completed years and additional months, plus the sex-specific growth reference, for ages 2 to under 20.

Select the measurement system before entering height and weight. In US mode, height is total inches: 5 feet 9 inches is 69 inches, not 5.9. The arithmetic uses the same physical measurements after unit conversion; switching units should not change the underlying BMI.

links.label: Open the child and teen calculation

sections.title: Work through BMI = weight divided by height squared
paragraphs: For a 30-year-old adult at 70 kg and 175 cm, convert height to 1.75 m, square it to obtain 3.0625 m², then divide 70 by 3.0625. The result is approximately 22.86 kg/m². Age selects the adult pathway; it does not appear in this formula.

A small height-entry error affects the denominator twice because height is squared. At the same 70 kg, entering 170 cm instead gives approximately 24.22. Recheck the measurement and units before interpreting a result near a category boundary.

table.caption: The same weight with three entered heights

sections.title: Read category boundaries without rounding the input into a new band
paragraphs: The adult screening intervals use exact boundaries: below 18.5; 18.5 to below 25; 25 to below 30; and 30 or above. The result is assigned from the calculated value, before display rounding. A value that displays as 25.00 can therefore require more precision to understand its boundary position.
The category describes one screening reference. BMI does not separate muscle, fat, bone or fluid, and a category alone does not establish someone’s health or identify an appropriate treatment.

sections.title: Understand what a child percentile compares
paragraphs: A BMI-for-age percentile compares a child’s BMI with the age- and sex-specific reference distribution. It is not a body-fat percentage. The example of 30 kg, 135 cm and 9 years 6 months in the male reference gives BMI about 16.46 and a percentile about 51.35.

Finflo uses CDC LMS data and the 2022 extended reference above the 95th percentile. Enter completed age carefully; changing months can change the percentile even when height and weight stay the same. Growth over time deserves more attention than an isolated calculator result.

links.label: CDC child and teen BMI categories
CDC data for the extended BMI-for-age growth charts

sections.title: Use BMI alongside the question you are actually trying to answer
paragraphs: For an adult height-based reference interval, use the Healthy Weight Calculator. For an estimate of body composition, a circumference equation answers a different question and has its own measurement limitations. Neither replaces a clinical assessment.

Adult category labels should not be applied to children, and pregnancy changes the interpretation of body weight. If a result seems surprising, check the entry first and discuss the measurement context with a qualified health professional.

links.label: Explore the adult height-based reference interval

bmi-calculator.seoTitle: BMI Calculator: Adult BMI & Child Percentiles

anorexic-bmi-calculator.description: Understand adult BMI and why it cannot diagnose anorexia, assess an eating disorder or establish an underweight target.

faqs.question: Is there an anorexic BMI cutoff I should aim for?
faqs.answer: No. This tool does not provide an underweight target or a number to aim for. BMI cannot determine whether someone has an eating disorder.

faqs.question: Can someone have an eating disorder with a BMI in the reference range?
faqs.answer: Yes. Body size alone cannot rule out an eating disorder or determine whether support is needed.

faqs.question: Why does this page show ordinary BMI?
faqs.answer: It explains the limited arithmetic behind a common search phrase. The output is an adult screening measure, not a diagnosis of anorexia.

faqs.question: Can this tell me whether I am eating enough?
faqs.answer: No. Height and weight do not describe nutritional intake, medical needs or eating behaviors.

faqs.question: Should a child use this mode?
faqs.answer: No. This adult mode starts at age 20. A child’s growth requires an age- and sex-specific reference and appropriate professional interpretation.

faqs.question: What if repeatedly checking BMI makes me more anxious?
faqs.answer: You can stop using the calculator and discuss the concern with a trusted person or qualified health professional. You do not need a particular result to ask for support.

sections.title: Why there is no BMI number that diagnoses an eating disorder
paragraphs: A search for an “anorexic BMI” can suggest that a single boundary decides whether someone is ill or deserves support. It does not. This page provides adult BMI arithmetic and explains its limits; it does not calculate a weight to reach, a restriction target or an eating-disorder diagnosis.

Eating disorders can affect people across body sizes. A result inside an adult reference range cannot rule out illness or make restrictive eating, purging or distress around food harmless. Concerns about eating or body image are worth discussing without waiting for a number to change.

links.label: NIMH: eating disorders and getting help

sections.title: What the displayed BMI actually measures
paragraphs: The formula is weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared. For example, 70 kg at 175 cm gives 70 ÷ 1.75² ≈ 22.86 kg/m². This explains the calculation only; it is not a goal or an assessment of a person’s eating patterns.
Use the measurement system shown in the form and total inches for a US height entry. This mode is for adults aged 20 and over. It does not provide pediatric growth interpretation.

table.caption: Information present and absent from a BMI calculation
rows: An eating-disorder diagnosis or need for care

sections.title: Separate a screening label from severity or eligibility for support
paragraphs: BMI does not show recent weight change, fluid status, laboratory results or the effects of eating behaviors on daily life. Two people with the same number can have very different histories and needs. Repeatedly checking a calculator cannot supply those missing details.

If checking numbers makes eating or body-image concerns harder to manage, it is reasonable to stop using the tool and talk with someone you trust or a qualified clinician. The calculation is optional; access to support is not something it can determine.

sections.title: Prepare useful context for a health conversation
paragraphs: Describe the changes or concerns that prompted the search: difficulties around meals, distress about food or body image, changes in energy, and how long the problem has been affecting you. A clinician can decide which history, examination or tests are relevant.

Avoid treating comparisons with online photos, someone else’s BMI or an equation output as evidence that a concern is too small to mention. The purpose of a clinical assessment is to understand the person, not to match a calculator label.

sections.title: Use the appropriate reference if the question is growth
paragraphs: For a child or teenager, adult BMI bands are not the appropriate comparison. A pediatric reference uses age and sex and should be considered with growth history. That reference still cannot diagnose an eating disorder or establish a weight-loss target.
The general BMI page explains adult versus child calculation methods. This page keeps the narrower focus on why BMI cannot answer the question implied by “anorexic BMI.”

links.label: Read how adult and child BMI calculations differ
CDC: the role of adult BMI as screening

anorexic-bmi-calculator.seoTitle: Adult BMI & Eating Disorders: Screening Information

overweight-calculator.description: Check adult BMI category boundaries, understand rounding near a cutoff, and choose the appropriate adult or child reference without setting a personal weight target.

faqs.question: What BMI band is called overweight for adults?
faqs.answer: The stated adult screening interval starts at 25 and ends below 30 kg/m². Finflo uses the unrounded calculation for the category.

faqs.question: Why can a result display 25.00 but remain below the boundary?
faqs.answer: A value such as 24.9969 rounds to 25.00 for display. Its underlying value is still below 25.

faqs.question: Is this appropriate during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Pregnancy changes the interpretation of body weight. Do not use an adult BMI category alone to assess pregnancy gain or set a goal.

faqs.question: Can a muscular adult fall in this band?
faqs.answer: Yes. BMI does not distinguish muscle from fat, so additional assessment may be needed.

faqs.question: Does this calculate how much weight I should lose?
faqs.answer: No. It reports screening arithmetic. Personal health decisions require more information than this category.

faqs.question: Which tool should a 16-year-old use?
faqs.answer: Use the Child & teen BMI-for-age mode in the BMI Calculator and interpret growth with appropriate clinical guidance.

sections.title: Use the result as an adult screening category
paragraphs: This tool calculates BMI and identifies the corresponding adult reference band. Enter age, height and weight, selecting metric or US units first. Adults aged 20 and over use this pathway; younger users need the separate BMI-for-age mode.

The word “overweight” here is the name of a screening interval, not a complete health assessment. The same BMI can reflect different amounts of muscle, fat or fluid. The calculator cannot decide whether a particular person needs to change weight.

sections.title: Check exactly where a boundary falls
paragraphs: At a height of 180 cm, the squared height is 3.24 m². A weight of 81 kg gives BMI 81 ÷ 3.24 = 25 exactly. A slightly smaller weight can produce a value below 25 even if rounding displays 25.00.
Finflo assigns the category before rounding the displayed BMI. The examples below use age 30, metric units and height 180 cm. They illustrate arithmetic around a threshold, not target weights.

table.caption: A boundary example at the same entered height

sections.title: Avoid common unit and measurement errors
paragraphs: Height must be centimeters in metric mode and total inches in US mode. Entering 1.80 into a centimeter field is not the same as entering 180. Likewise, 5.10 is a decimal value, not shorthand for 5 feet 10 inches.

Use a consistent measurement method when comparing dates. Ordinary rounding of height or weight can move a displayed result near a boundary. Keep the original measurements when a precise comparison matters.

sections.title: Understand what BMI leaves out
paragraphs: The formula contains only weight and squared height; it cannot describe fat distribution or physical fitness. Pregnancy and unusually high muscle mass are examples of situations requiring additional context.

A category boundary does not mark an abrupt biological change at the last decimal place. Interpret changes alongside relevant medical history and other health information instead of treating the label as a standalone diagnosis.

sections.title: Choose the next calculation for the right reason
paragraphs: Use the main BMI Calculator for child and teen percentiles. The Healthy Weight Calculator reverses the adult reference formula for a selected height; it does not prescribe a personal goal. Circumference-based body-fat estimates are another model, not a more definitive diagnosis.
If your concern is a recent unexplained change or a health symptom, another online calculation cannot resolve its cause. A qualified health professional can assess the context the formula lacks.

overweight-calculator.seoTitle: Overweight Calculator: Adult BMI Screening Categories

bmr-calculator.description: Estimate adult resting energy expenditure using the available equations, and convert food energy between kilocalories and kilojoules.

faqs.question: Is BMR the number of calories I should eat?
faqs.answer: No. This output estimates resting expenditure and does not include the complete daily activity context or individual nutrition needs.

faqs.question: Which equation requires body-fat percentage?
faqs.answer: Katch–McArdle uses estimated lean mass, so it requires body-fat percentage. The other two equations here use height, weight, age and sex category.

faqs.question: Why is there no activity selector in the resting-energy mode?
faqs.answer: Activity belongs in an estimate of total daily energy expenditure. The BMR mode keeps the resting calculation separate.

faqs.question: Does 1 kcal mean 1 food Calorie?
faqs.answer: Yes. A dietary Calorie is a kilocalorie; 1 kcal equals 4.184 kJ using the conversion applied here.

faqs.question: Can I use a result with two decimals as an exact metabolic measurement?
faqs.answer: No. Decimal precision reflects arithmetic, not biological certainty or an individual laboratory measurement.

faqs.question: Can this be used for a child or during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: These adult estimates are not intended for children, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Use appropriate clinical nutrition guidance instead.

sections.title: Distinguish resting energy from a full day of energy use
paragraphs: This BMR calculator estimates resting energy expenditure with Mifflin–St Jeor, revised Harris–Benedict or Katch–McArdle. Choose an equation and enter the measurements it requires. Katch–McArdle additionally uses the entered body-fat percentage.

Resting energy is not the same as daily maintenance energy or a recommended food intake. The resting equation does not include the full effect of movement and other daily activity. Use TDEE when you want to add an explicit activity assumption.

sections.title: Check the Mifflin–St Jeor example term by term
paragraphs: For the male equation at age 30, weight 70 kg and height 175 cm, the arithmetic is 10 × 70 + 6.25 × 175 − 5 × 30 + 5. That equals 1,648.75 kcal/day. The female equation uses −161 in place of +5 for the same numerical measurements.

The table shows each contribution rather than implying the decimal result is a precise measurement of metabolism. A predictive equation can produce many digits even when the biological estimate is uncertain.

table.caption: Mifflin–St Jeor arithmetic for the initial male example

links.label: Mifflin and colleagues: original resting-energy study

sections.title: Understand why choosing another equation changes the estimate
paragraphs: For the same 70 kg, 175 cm, age-30 male input, revised Harris–Benedict gives about 1,695.67 kcal/day. Katch–McArdle with body fat entered as 20% gives 370 + 21.6 × 56 = 1,579.6 kcal/day, because the estimated lean mass is 56 kg.

Katch’s body-fat input adds another measurement assumption. Guessing a body-fat percentage just to use that equation does not make the result more individualized or more accurate. Compare methods only with their input differences clearly stated.

links.label: Published equations and their population limitations

sections.title: Keep measurement units and food-energy units separate
paragraphs: Metric inputs use kilograms and centimeters. US height is total inches and US weight is pounds. The equation is evaluated in its required units after conversion, so unit selection changes how measurements are entered, not the physiology being modeled.
A dietary Calorie is one kilocalorie. To express 1,648.75 kcal in kilojoules, multiply by 4.184 to get 6,898.37 kJ. The food-energy converter also distinguishes small calories from kilocalories.

sections.title: Recognize when a resting estimate is not an appropriate intake rule
paragraphs: This implementation accepts adult energy inputs from age 20. It is not a model for children, pregnancy, breastfeeding or individualized medical nutrition care. A clinical measurement of resting expenditure is a different procedure from applying a population equation.

Do not interpret the result as a universal minimum, maximum or daily eating target. For a transparent maintenance scenario, carry the resting estimate into an activity-adjusted calculation and keep the added assumption visible.

bmr-calculator.seoTitle: BMR Calculator: Estimate Adult Resting Energy

calorie-calculator.description: Estimate daily maintenance calories with Mifflin–St Jeor, Harris–Benedict or Katch–McArdle. Compare activity assumptions and convert kcal to kJ.
calorie-calculator.seoTitle: Calorie Calculator: Daily Calories, BMR & TDEE

sections.title: Calculate daily maintenance calories from resting energy
paragraphs: This calorie calculator estimates maintenance energy by multiplying a resting-energy estimate by the activity factor you select. Maintenance means the modeled energy needed to keep body weight broadly stable under those assumptions. It is different from the energy used at rest, often called BMR or RMR, and from a meal plan for an individual.

Choose Daily energy to enter body measurements and an equation. The result separates estimated maintenance energy, resting energy and maintenance energy in kilojoules. Choose Food energy conversion for kcal and kJ, or Calories, kilocalories & joules when you also need small calories or joules. The daily-energy form is for adults age 20 and above; it does not model pregnancy, breastfeeding or children.

links.label: Enter measurements for a daily energy estimate

sections.title: Work through the calorie calculator’s starting example
paragraphs: The opening example uses age 30, the male equation coefficient, 70 kg, 175 cm and Mifflin–St Jeor. Its resting estimate is 10 × 70 + 6.25 × 175 − 5 × 30 + 5 = 1,648.75 kcal/day. Selecting Sedentary multiplies that result by 1.2: 1,648.75 × 1.2 = 1,978.50 kcal/day.

Changing Activity level to Resting energy only selects a factor of 1, so the main result becomes 1,648.75 kcal/day. That setting removes the activity allowance; it does not describe the full energy needs of an ordinary day. The two decimal places make the arithmetic reproducible, not a claim that a person’s daily expenditure is known to that precision.

table.caption: Separate the two stages of the 30-year-old example

links.label: Mifflin et al.: the original resting-energy study

sections.title: Compare the three available calorie equations
paragraphs: Mifflin–St Jeor and revised Harris–Benedict use weight, height, age and the selected sex coefficient. Katch–McArdle instead uses estimated lean mass, calculated from weight and body-fat percentage. Selecting Katch–McArdle reveals the Body fat field. Replace its example value with an appropriate estimate; the prefilled 20% is not a measurement of you.

For the same 30-year-old example, the equations give the results below. Katch–McArdle additionally assumes 20% body fat, so lean mass is 70 × 0.8 = 56 kg and resting energy is 370 + 21.6 × 56 = 1,579.60 kcal/day. These differences illustrate model choice. The range between equations is not a measured error bound, and choosing the largest or smallest result does not establish which estimate fits an individual.

table.caption: Same example measurements and 1.2 activity factor; Katch also assumes 20% body fat

links.label: Roza and Shizgal: revised Harris–Benedict research
Published comparison of resting-energy equations, Table 1

sections.title: See how the activity assumption changes maintenance calories
paragraphs: Activity factors describe scenarios, not a direct measurement from a workout count. The labels are a starting point for identifying an assumption; duration, intensity, work and movement outside exercise can differ even when two people exercise on the same number of days. Compare nearby settings if you are unsure which scenario represents your usual routine.

The table holds resting energy at 1,648.75 kcal/day and changes only the multiplier. Moving from Light to Moderate raises the result by about 289 kcal/day. That difference comes entirely from the selected assumption. The activity-adjusted estimate already includes an allowance for movement, so automatically adding a separate workout estimate can count some activity twice.

table.caption: Activity scenarios for the same example, rounded to the nearest whole kcal
rows: Highly active: demanding work and training

links.label: Explore daily expenditure in the TDEE calculator
Estimate energy for a specified activity separately

sections.title: Enter pounds and total inches correctly
paragraphs: Metric mode uses kilograms and centimeters. US mode uses pounds and total inches, so a height of 5 feet 9 inches is entered as 5 × 12 + 9 = 69 inches. Entering 5.9 does not mean 5 feet 9 inches. Changing Measurement system converts the existing weight and height entries; inspect the displayed units before editing the converted numbers.

For an equivalent-unit check, 70 kg is about 154.3236 lb and 175 cm is about 68.8976 inches. Entering those equivalents with the same age, equation and activity factor should reproduce the same energy estimate apart from rounding. A result that changes substantially after a unit switch is a reason to check what the numbers represent.

links.label: Convert feet and inches before entering height

sections.title: Convert Calories, kcal and kJ without a thousandfold error
paragraphs: A food Calorie is one kilocalorie, written kcal. Finflo uses the thermochemical conversion: 1 kcal = 4.184 kJ = 4,184 J. A small calorie, written cal, is one-thousandth of a kcal. Do not interpret a food label’s 250 Calories as 250 small calories.

To convert a kilojoule label to kcal, divide by 4.184; to convert kcal to kJ, multiply by 4.184. In Calories, kilocalories & joules, enter the amount and select its input unit. The four outputs describe the same energy, not four amounts to add together.

table.caption: Equivalent food-energy amounts using the thermochemical calorie

links.label: Convert between all four energy units
NIST: calorie and joule conversion factors

sections.title: Match the serving size before comparing food labels
paragraphs: Consider an illustrative label showing 180 kcal per 45 g serving. A 67.5 g portion contains 67.5 ÷ 45 = 1.5 labeled servings, so its energy is 180 × 1.5 = 270 kcal, equivalent to 1,129.68 kJ. Comparing the label’s 180 kcal directly with a different portion would compare different quantities.

If another label gives energy per 100 g, put both labels on that basis first. In this example, 180 ÷ 45 × 100 = 400 kcal per 100 g. A serving size describes the basis of the label; it is not a personal recommendation. Likewise, the 2,000-calorie reference used on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels is general nutrition guidance, not an individualized maintenance estimate.

table.caption: One illustrative food label expressed for different amounts

links.label: FDA: serving information and Calories on food labels

sections.title: Know what a maintenance estimate cannot predict
paragraphs: This page estimates energy for the measurements and activity scenario you enter. It does not calculate a weight-loss deadline, guarantee a particular weight change, or decide an appropriate intake for a person with medical or nutritional needs. A fixed calories-per-pound rule cannot account for changing energy expenditure and body composition over time.

NIDDK’s Body Weight Planner uses a different, dynamic model for adult weight-change scenarios. Its planning assumptions should not be mixed with this page’s simple activity multipliers as though the methods were identical. For pregnancy, breastfeeding, childhood growth or medical nutrition care, use advice specific to those circumstances rather than adapting this maintenance calculator.

links.label: NIDDK: why static weight-change rules miss metabolic changes
NIDDK: Body Weight Planner and its scope

faqs.question: How many calories do I need per day to maintain weight?
faqs.answer: This calculator estimates maintenance calories from a resting-energy equation and an activity factor. Enter your own measurements and compare the assumptions; there is no single daily calorie number that applies to everyone. The result is an estimate rather than a prescribed intake.

faqs.question: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE in this calculator?
faqs.answer: The resting-energy result estimates energy used at rest. The maintenance or TDEE result multiplies that estimate by the selected activity factor. Choosing Resting energy only sets the multiplier to 1 and excludes the activity allowance.

faqs.question: Which calorie equation should I use if I do not know my body-fat percentage?
faqs.answer: Mifflin–St Jeor and revised Harris–Benedict run without a body-fat input. Katch–McArdle requires one because it estimates lean mass. Its prefilled body-fat percentage is an example, not a measurement; do not assume it describes you.

faqs.question: Why do different calorie calculators give different answers?
faqs.answer: Check the equation, activity multiplier, age, measurements and units first. A different coefficient or activity assumption changes the result even when both calculators implement their formulas correctly. Extra decimal places do not resolve the uncertainty in those assumptions.

faqs.question: Can I enter height in feet and inches?
faqs.answer: The US setting accepts total inches. Convert feet to inches and add the remaining inches: 5 feet 9 inches is 69 inches. Metric mode accepts centimeters. The separate Height Calculator can convert a feet-and-inches measurement.

faqs.question: Are Calories and kcal the same on a food label?
faqs.answer: Yes. One food Calorie equals 1 kcal, or 4.184 kJ using the thermochemical convention. It is also 1,000 small calories. Match the serving size as well as the energy unit when comparing labels.

faqs.question: Should I add exercise calories to the maintenance result?
faqs.answer: The selected activity factor already adds an allowance above resting energy. Automatically adding a workout estimate can count overlapping activity twice. Keep the assumptions separate and check what each estimate includes.

faqs.question: Does this calculator set a calorie deficit or predict a weight-loss date?
faqs.answer: No. It estimates maintenance energy under fixed inputs and converts food-energy units. Weight-change predictions need additional assumptions about time and changing expenditure; a fixed daily subtraction does not guarantee a specific outcome.

faqs.question: Can children, pregnant people or breastfeeding people use this estimate?
faqs.answer: The daily-energy form starts at age 20 and does not model growth, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Those circumstances, and medical nutrition care, require an appropriate assessment rather than this general maintenance estimate.

tdee-calculator.description: Estimate total daily energy expenditure by combining an adult resting-energy equation with your selected activity factor.

faqs.question: How is TDEE different from BMR?
faqs.answer: BMR or resting energy is the starting estimate. TDEE here multiplies it by a selected activity factor to model a fuller day of expenditure.

faqs.question: What does the factor of 1 mean?
faqs.answer: It reports resting energy only. It is not a typical complete daily maintenance scenario.

faqs.question: Why do calculators show different maintenance calories?
faqs.answer: They may use different resting equations, activity factors, units or body-fat assumptions. Compare those inputs before comparing totals.

faqs.question: Should I add my watch’s workout calories to this result?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. An activity factor already allows for movement, and workout estimates may include resting energy. Check for double counting.

faqs.question: Does this predict how quickly my weight will change?
faqs.answer: No. It estimates an expenditure scenario rather than a body-weight trajectory or prescribed calorie deficit.

faqs.question: Why does changing US to metric units not change the answer?
faqs.answer: Equivalent measurements describe the same body inputs. The equations require normalized units, so conversion should preserve the estimate.

sections.title: Build a daily expenditure estimate in two visible steps
paragraphs: TDEE stands for total daily energy expenditure. This calculator first estimates resting energy from your selected adult equation, then multiplies that result by an activity factor. Enter measurements, choose the equation and select the activity assumption before calculating.

The returned maintenance estimate is the modeled total, while the resting estimate is shown separately. Keeping both numbers visible helps distinguish changes caused by body measurements from changes caused only by the activity setting.

sections.title: Reproduce a maintenance scenario from the resting estimate
paragraphs: For a male equation input at age 30, 70 kg and 175 cm, Mifflin–St Jeor gives 1,648.75 kcal/day at rest. With the 1.2 sedentary factor, modeled maintenance is 1,648.75 × 1.2 = 1,978.5 kcal/day.
Selecting 1.55 instead produces 2,555.5625 kcal/day with the same resting estimate. That difference is entirely due to the activity assumption; it is not evidence that measured metabolism changed.

table.caption: Hold resting energy fixed and change only the activity factor

sections.title: Choose activity assumptions without counting exercise twice
paragraphs: The labels describe rough scenarios. Exercise duration and intensity, physically demanding work and movement outside exercise can differ greatly among people with the same number of weekly workouts. Comparing neighboring factors makes that uncertainty visible.

An activity-adjusted daily total already includes an allowance for movement. Adding an entire workout estimate on top without checking what the factor already represents can double count energy. Activity estimates may also report gross energy, which includes a resting component.

links.label: Understand gross versus above-resting activity energy

sections.title: Keep equation choice and unit conversion in the comparison
paragraphs: Mifflin–St Jeor, revised Harris–Benedict and Katch–McArdle use different predictors or coefficients. Katch requires body-fat percentage. If comparing results across tools, check the equation, inputs and factor before attributing the discrepancy to an error.

Metric measurements are kilograms and centimeters; US height is total inches. Maintenance energy in kJ is the kcal result multiplied by 4.184, so converting units should preserve the underlying scenario.

sections.title: Treat maintenance as an estimate rather than a weight-change forecast
paragraphs: A calculated TDEE does not guarantee that body weight will remain unchanged at that intake, and it does not predict a specific date of weight change. Individual expenditure and reporting accuracy vary over time.

The energy modes here are for adults from age 20 and exclude pregnancy, breastfeeding, growing children and individualized medical nutrition care. The Calorie Calculator provides additional food-label and unit examples without turning a maintenance estimate into a prescribed deficit.

links.label: Read the fuller calorie and food-energy guide

tdee-calculator.seoTitle: TDEE Calculator: Estimate Daily Energy Expenditure

macro-calculator.description: Convert a daily energy target into protein, carbohydrate and fat grams, or explore adult reference ranges from body measurements.

faqs.question: Why must the percentages total 100?
faqs.answer: They divide the entered energy amount among three macronutrients. A complete allocation must account for all of that amount once.

faqs.question: Why does fat produce fewer grams for the same calories?
faqs.answer: This arithmetic uses about 9 kcal per gram of fat and 4 per gram of protein or carbohydrate.

faqs.question: Can I choose all the upper gram ranges?
faqs.answer: No. The upper energy-share endpoints sum to more than 100%, so they do not form one complete split.

faqs.question: Is the 2,000 kcal starting value my recommendation?
faqs.answer: No. It is an illustrative input. The calculator does not establish an individual energy prescription.

faqs.question: Is 20% protein the same as 20 grams?
faqs.answer: No. At 2,000 kcal, 20% is 400 kcal from protein, which is 100 grams using 4 kcal/g.

faqs.question: Does the result account for fiber and food quality?
faqs.answer: It does not create a complete dietary assessment. Nutrient composition and label conventions can require more detail than this energy split.

sections.title: Choose between splitting an entered energy amount and estimating reference ranges
paragraphs: Daily macronutrients divides an energy amount among protein, carbohydrate and fat using percentages you enter. From body measurements & activity first estimates adult energy expenditure, then displays independent population reference ranges. These modes answer different questions.

For a specified split, all three percentages must total 100. Use the energy amount relevant to your own planning context; the 2,000 kcal starting value is an arithmetic example, not a personal intake recommendation.

sections.title: Convert energy shares into grams correctly
paragraphs: Protein and carbohydrate use approximately 4 kcal per gram; fat uses approximately 9 kcal per gram. Multiply total kcal by each percentage divided by 100, then divide that nutrient’s kcal by its conversion factor.

At 2,000 kcal with 20% protein, 50% carbohydrate and 30% fat, the results are 100 g protein, 250 g carbohydrate and about 66.67 g fat. The gram totals do not need to add to 100 or 2,000; the energy shares do.

table.caption: A complete illustrative 20/50/30 split

links.label: Health Canada: dietary reference values for macronutrients

sections.title: Do not combine every upper reference endpoint into one diet
paragraphs: The adult energy-share ranges shown by the reference mode are carbohydrate 45–65%, fat 20–35% and protein 10–35%. These are separate ranges. Their lower endpoints add to 75%, while their upper endpoints add to 135%.

Consequently, choosing all upper gram values would exceed the modeled energy amount. A complete chosen split must still total 100%; a range display is not three independent instructions to maximize intake.

sections.title: Check the energy estimate before interpreting its nutrient outputs
paragraphs: The body-measurement mode uses a selected resting equation and activity factor. Its optional Daily energy adjustment changes the scenario explicitly; it does not predict a weight-loss rate or make that adjusted intake appropriate for an individual.
Changing the activity factor changes every energy-based gram range. By contrast, a grams-per-kilogram protein calculation uses a different basis and is available in the Protein Calculator.

links.label: Compare protein grams from body weight

sections.title: Use macro arithmetic without overlooking food composition
paragraphs: The result gives quantities, not a menu or a judgment of diet quality. It does not select foods, check micronutrients or account for every food-label rounding convention. Meal composition, fiber and individual medical needs require information beyond these three totals.

The adult reference-energy mode is not intended for children, pregnancy, breastfeeding or individualized medical nutrition care. A nutrition professional can help interpret an appropriate plan when health conditions or dietary restrictions are relevant.

macro-calculator.seoTitle: Macro Calculator: Protein, Carbohydrate & Fat Grams

carbohydrate-calculator.description: Estimate carbohydrate grams from a calorie target and percentage, or explore adult energy-based carbohydrate reference ranges.

faqs.question: How many grams are 50% of 2,000 calories?
faqs.answer: The carbohydrate share is 1,000 kcal. Dividing by approximately 4 kcal/g gives 250 g.

faqs.question: Why must I also enter protein and fat percentages?
faqs.answer: The Daily macronutrients mode checks that the complete energy allocation totals 100%.

faqs.question: Does this calculate net carbs?
faqs.answer: No. It converts a carbohydrate energy share into grams and does not subtract fiber or sugar alcohols.

faqs.question: Is this a diabetes meal-planning prescription?
faqs.answer: No. It does not assess medication, glucose measurements or individual clinical nutrition needs.

faqs.question: What does the 45–65% range mean?
faqs.answer: It is the adult population reference energy-share range used by this mode, not an instruction to choose every maximum shown.

faqs.question: Can I use kcal and kJ interchangeably in the energy field?
faqs.answer: No. The field requests kcal. Convert kJ to kcal first; 1 kcal equals 4.184 kJ.

sections.title: Translate a carbohydrate energy share into daily grams
paragraphs: Use Daily macronutrients when you already have an energy amount and want to calculate the carbohydrate share. Enter total kcal and percentages for protein, carbohydrate and fat; all three shares must total 100 even though carbohydrate is highlighted first.

Carbohydrate grams = total kcal × carbohydrate percentage ÷ 100 ÷ 4. The result is the quantity corresponding to your entered assumptions, not a diagnosis, carbohydrate restriction or personalized nutrition prescription.

sections.title: Compare carbohydrate percentages at the same energy amount
paragraphs: At an illustrative 2,000 kcal, a 50% carbohydrate share gives 1,000 kcal from carbohydrate and 250 g. A 45% share gives 225 g, while 65% gives 325 g. When changing carbohydrate share in the form, adjust the other percentages so the total remains 100.
The table isolates the carbohydrate arithmetic. It does not recommend that a particular person select the lowest or highest value.

table.caption: Carbohydrate examples at a fixed 2,000 kcal

sections.title: Read the body-measurement mode as a range of assumptions
paragraphs: From body measurements & activity calculates an adult maintenance-energy scenario and displays the carbohydrate reference range from 45–65% of scenario energy. At the initial 1,978.5 kcal example, that is approximately 222.6–321.5 g/day.
The range moves if the selected equation, activity factor or energy adjustment changes. It does not measure carbohydrate use during a workout or prescribe a value for diabetes management.

sections.title: Distinguish total carbohydrate from food-label subcategories
paragraphs: The calculator’s grams are an energy-based arithmetic quantity. It does not subtract fiber or sugar alcohols to create a “net carb” figure, and it does not determine the amount of added sugar in a meal.

When using a food label, match the listed serving size to the portion actually considered. Multiplying a carbohydrate value by the number of servings is separate from deciding which labeling convention applies in your country.

sections.title: Keep energy, portions and clinical advice in their proper roles
paragraphs: Daily grams and grams per meal are different quantities. Dividing a daily amount by three, for example, is a mathematical distribution choice, not proof that every meal should contain equal carbohydrate.

Medical nutrition needs, pregnancy, breastfeeding and childhood are outside the adult energy model’s scope. For those contexts, use qualified guidance rather than inferring a treatment target from a percentage calculation.

links.label: See all three macronutrient shares together
Understand food Calories and serving sizes

carbohydrate-calculator.seoTitle: Carbohydrate Calculator: Calories to Daily Grams

fat-intake-calculator.description: Convert a selected share of daily calories into fat grams and compare adult energy-based fat-intake reference ranges.

faqs.question: How do I convert fat calories into grams?
faqs.answer: Divide fat calories by approximately 9. For example, 600 kcal from fat corresponds to about 66.67 g.

faqs.question: Is dietary fat the same as body-fat percentage?
faqs.answer: No. This tool converts an energy share into dietary grams; body-fat percentage describes estimated body composition.

faqs.question: Does the output specify saturated fat?
faqs.answer: No. It reports total fat represented by the entered energy share and does not divide it into fatty-acid categories.

faqs.question: Why is the fat gram total smaller than carbohydrate for equal calories?
faqs.answer: The conversion factors differ: approximately 9 kcal/g for fat versus 4 kcal/g for carbohydrate.

faqs.question: Can all reference-range maxima be combined?
faqs.answer: No. The nutrient ranges are independent; a complete selected energy allocation must still total 100%.

faqs.question: Does this decide an appropriate fat intake for me?
faqs.answer: No. The amount follows your assumptions and the selected population reference. It is not an individual nutrition prescription.

sections.title: Calculate fat grams from an entered energy percentage
paragraphs: Daily macronutrients converts a selected fat share into grams while retaining protein and carbohydrate for a complete 100% allocation. Start with the entered kcal amount, multiply by the fat percentage divided by 100, then divide by approximately 9 kcal per gram.
This estimates total dietary fat represented by the energy split. It does not measure body fat or determine how much body fat someone will gain or lose.

sections.title: Reproduce a 30% fat-share example
paragraphs: For 2,000 kcal and a 30% fat share, fat supplies 600 kcal. Dividing 600 by 9 gives 66.6667 g, displayed as about 66.67 g. With protein at 20% and carbohydrate at 50%, all three shares sum to 100%.
Rounding the result to whole grams can change the reconstructed energy slightly. Keep extra precision during arithmetic and round only at the display or reporting stage.

table.caption: Total-fat arithmetic at an illustrative 2,000 kcal

links.label: Health Canada adult macronutrient reference values

sections.title: Understand the separate body-measurement reference mode
paragraphs: From body measurements & activity estimates scenario energy and applies the adult fat-energy reference range of 20–35%. At the initial 1,978.5 kcal scenario, that produces approximately 44.0–76.9 g/day.
Those endpoints are a range for one nutrient. Combining upper endpoints for fat, protein and carbohydrate would exceed the same energy amount, so the results are not a ready-made diet.

sections.title: Do not confuse total fat with saturated fat or food weight
paragraphs: A total-fat result does not specify saturated, unsaturated or trans-fat quantities. It also does not translate directly into the weight of a food: most foods contain water and other nutrients as well as fat.
For example, a portion labeled with 10 g of total fat contributes approximately 90 kcal from fat under this arithmetic. That does not imply the entire portion weighs 10 g or supplies only 90 kcal.

sections.title: Use the conversion within its nutrition-planning limits
paragraphs: Changing the selected calorie amount changes the gram estimate proportionally. The calculation cannot establish whether the entered energy amount or nutrient allocation meets an individual’s needs.

Children, pregnancy, breastfeeding and medical nutrition care require context beyond this adult reference model. Use the result to understand an energy split, and get appropriate guidance when deciding what that split should be.

links.label: Compare protein, carbohydrate and fat in one calculation

fat-intake-calculator.seoTitle: Fat Intake Calculator: Calories to Daily Fat Grams

protein-calculator.description: Estimate daily protein grams from body weight and a chosen g/kg target, or compare adult energy-based protein reference ranges.

faqs.question: How much protein does 0.8 g/kg give at 70 kg?
faqs.answer: The arithmetic gives 70 × 0.8 = 56 g/day. Whether that reference is appropriate depends on the person’s context.

faqs.question: Does the factor change to grams per pound in US mode?
faqs.answer: No. Weight converts from pounds to kilograms; the factor remains g/kg/day.

faqs.question: Is 100 g of a food the same as 100 g of protein?
faqs.answer: No. A food’s total weight includes its other components. Use the protein amount on its label or a suitable composition source.

faqs.question: Why does the energy-range method give a different answer?
faqs.answer: It converts a share of estimated calories into grams, whereas the basic method multiplies body weight by a chosen g/kg factor.

faqs.question: Does a higher factor automatically produce a better plan?
faqs.answer: No. It produces a larger number mathematically but does not establish that the amount is suitable or beneficial.

faqs.question: Can this set protein intake for kidney disease?
faqs.answer: No. Medical nutrition needs should be assessed by qualified professionals; the calculator is not a treatment-planning tool.

sections.title: Choose body-weight arithmetic or an energy-based reference
paragraphs: Daily protein multiplies weight in kilograms by the entered grams-per-kilogram-per-day factor. From body measurements & activity instead converts a percentage range of estimated energy into grams. These methods use different denominators and should not be treated as interchangeable.

The starting factor of 0.8 g/kg/day represents the adult RDA reference used here. It is not a universal target for every age, activity pattern, pregnancy or medical condition. The calculator allows an explicit factor without deciding which factor is appropriate for you.

links.label: Health Canada dietary reference values for protein

sections.title: Check a 70 kg example and the units of the factor
paragraphs: At 70 kg and 0.8 g/kg/day, the calculation is 70 × 0.8 = 56 g/day. If you enter pounds, choose US units so weight is converted to kilograms before multiplication.
The factor remains grams per kilogram, even in US mode. A factor expressed per pound must be converted before entry; otherwise the result answers a different question.

table.caption: Protein arithmetic under explicitly chosen example factors

sections.title: Why grams per kilogram and percentage of calories differ
paragraphs: At 2,000 kcal, a 20% protein share represents 400 kcal, or 100 g using approximately 4 kcal/g. At 70 kg, those 100 g are about 1.43 g/kg/day. The two descriptions can represent the same quantity only after both body weight and energy are specified.

The adult energy-reference mode displays a 10–35% protein-energy range. Its endpoints are not a substitute for an individual grams-per-kilogram recommendation, and the upper endpoints of all macronutrient ranges cannot be combined into one 100% allocation.

sections.title: Read daily grams separately from food portion weights
paragraphs: A result of 56 g/day refers to protein, not to 56 g of a particular food. Food portions include water, fat, carbohydrate and other material. Use the protein content per serving on an appropriate label when doing a portion calculation.
For an arithmetic example, if one serving lists 12 g protein, two servings contain 24 g. Counting that contribution is different from deciding how to distribute a daily quantity across meals.

sections.title: Check the assumption before using the answer as a plan
paragraphs: The body-weight method scales linearly: doubling the entered factor doubles the calculated grams. That mathematical behavior does not establish a benefit from a higher factor.

Kidney disease, pregnancy, growth, recovery from illness and other clinical contexts can require individualized guidance. The tool does not assess those conditions, recommend supplements or determine whether a diet is nutritionally adequate.

links.label: Understand the energy estimate used by the range mode

protein-calculator.seoTitle: Protein Calculator: Daily Grams from Weight or Energy

body-fat-calculator.description: Estimate body-fat percentage using historical circumference equations or the age- and sex-adjusted BMI study model.

faqs.question: Is BMI the same as body-fat percentage?
faqs.answer: No. BMI is weight divided by squared height. The BMI-based body-fat mode adds age and a sex coefficient to estimate a percentage; it does not directly measure body fat.

faqs.question: Why does the female circumference equation ask for hips?
faqs.answer: Its published regression uses waist plus hip minus neck, while the male equation uses waist minus neck.

faqs.question: Can I enter centimeters in the Navy equation?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select metric units and enter centimeters. The calculator converts the measurements to inches before applying the formula.

faqs.question: Why do the two methods disagree?
faqs.answer: One uses circumferences and height, while the other uses BMI, age and a sex coefficient. Different assumptions and measurement errors can produce different estimates.

faqs.question: Is estimated lean mass the amount of muscle I have?
faqs.answer: No. It includes all mass assigned to the non-fat compartment by this calculation, including water, organs and bone.

faqs.question: Does this result determine military eligibility?
faqs.answer: No. A historical body-fat regression does not establish compliance with current military policy or replace an official assessment.

sections.title: Choose a circumference estimate or a BMI-based equation
paragraphs: The circumference mode estimates body-fat percentage from height, neck and waist; the female equation also uses hip circumference. Enter weight to translate the estimated percentage into fat mass and lean mass. Metric inputs are converted to the inch-based measurements required by the formula.

The separate BMI-based mode uses height, weight, age and the equation’s sex coefficient. It offers an adult/adolescent equation for ages 16–83 and a distinct child equation for ages 7–15. These are the supported equation ranges, not proof that the estimate is accurate for every person within them.

sections.title: Worked circumference example
paragraphs: Choose male, metric units, height 175 cm, weight 70 kg, waist 85 cm and neck 38 cm. The circumference equation gives about 17.01%. Multiplying 70 kg by 0.170077 gives about 11.91 kg estimated fat mass; the remaining 58.09 kg is estimated lean mass.

table.caption: The same estimate expressed three ways

sections.title: What the formulas are doing
paragraphs: For the male circumference equation, body fat % = 86.010 × log₁₀(waist − neck) − 70.041 × log₁₀(height) + 36.76, with all lengths in inches. For the female equation, body fat % = 163.205 × log₁₀(waist + hip − neck) − 97.684 × log₁₀(height) − 78.387. The measurements inside each logarithm must be positive.

The adult BMI-based equation is 1.20 × BMI + 0.23 × age − 10.8 × maleFlag − 5.4, where maleFlag is 1 for the male coefficient and 0 for the female coefficient. For a 45-year-old male at 70 kg and 175 cm, it gives about 21.58%. That differs from the circumference example because the two equations use different predictors.

sections.title: Make comparisons with consistent measurements
paragraphs: Choose one method and repeat its measurement locations and units when comparing results. Moving a tape to a different waist location or changing tape tension can change the estimate without an equivalent change in body composition. Do not substitute a trouser size for a measured circumference.

The circumference calculation is a historical estimation method. It is not the current Army assessment or a substitute for an official measurement protocol. The BMI equation also cannot observe muscle, hydration or fat distribution directly.

sections.title: Interpret percentage and mass without treating them as goals
paragraphs: Body-fat percentage is a share of total mass; fat mass is that share expressed in kilograms or pounds. Lean mass includes water, organs, bone and other tissues, so it is not the same as skeletal muscle mass. Extra decimal places show the arithmetic, not the accuracy of a tape-based or BMI-based estimate.

A difference between methods does not identify which result is correct for an individual. If the result would affect medical care or is causing distress, discuss the measurement method and its limitations with a qualified professional rather than pursuing a calculated percentage.

body-fat-calculator.seoTitle: Body Fat Calculator: Circumference & BMI Estimates

army-body-fat-calculator.description: Compare the 2026 Army waist-to-height threshold using recorded measurements, or explore the historical 2023 body-fat equation.

faqs.question: Is the current output a body-fat percentage?
faqs.answer: No. The default 2026 mode reports recorded waist divided by recorded height, truncated to three decimal places.

faqs.question: Do I round 0.542857 to 0.543?
faqs.answer: No. Under the implemented recording rule, it becomes 0.542 because the fourth and later decimal places are discarded.

faqs.question: Does 0.550 meet the stated numerical threshold?
faqs.answer: The stated threshold is below 0.550, so equality is not below it. Official assessment procedures and decisions remain outside the calculator.

faqs.question: Can I use a single waist measurement?
faqs.answer: The input asks for the recorded average from the prescribed procedure. The calculator cannot confirm how a measurement was taken.

faqs.question: Why is the 2023 body-fat equation still available?
faqs.answer: It allows older calculations to be understood and reproduced. It is explicitly historical and does not determine current compliance.

faqs.question: Can this certify an Army assessment?
faqs.answer: No. It checks arithmetic from supplied measurements; it cannot verify measurement technique, eligibility, exemptions or official outcomes.

sections.title: Start with the policy version you need
paragraphs: The default mode applies the recorded waist-to-height arithmetic in Army Directive 2026-13 implementation guidance. It reports a ratio, not a body-fat percentage. Enter the recorded height and recorded average waist from the prescribed measurement process in inches.

A separate historical mode reproduces the 2023 one-site circumference equation. It remains useful for understanding older calculations, but its percentage does not determine compliance with the 2026 ratio policy.

sections.title: The 2026 ratio truncates at three decimal places
paragraphs: Divide the recorded average waist by recorded height, then retain the first three decimal places without rounding up. The stated numerical threshold is below 0.550. A value exactly equal to 0.550 is not below that threshold.

For recorded height 70 inches and recorded average waist 35 inches, 35 ÷ 70 = 0.500. The calculation returns the recorded ratio, the untruncated ratio and its relationship to the stated threshold. It does not decide exemptions, confirmation requirements or personnel outcomes.

table.caption: Arithmetic examples using already recorded measurements

sections.title: Why recorded measurements matter
paragraphs: Official guidance defines how measurements are taken, repeated and recorded before the ratio is calculated. A single casual tape reading is not interchangeable with that recorded average. This tool accepts the final recorded values; it does not verify that the measurement procedure was followed.

Both inputs must use the same length unit. This mode specifically expects inches because it follows the recorded-measurement workflow. Do not enter centimeters into a field labeled inches or mix a rounded height from one record with a waist from another assessment.

sections.title: How the historical 2023 equation differs
paragraphs: The older male equation is −26.97 − 0.12 × weight in pounds + 1.99 × abdominal circumference in inches. The older female equation is −9.15 − 0.015 × weight in pounds + 1.27 × abdominal circumference in inches. Metric inputs in that mode are converted before calculation.

A male example of 70 kg and 85 cm abdominal circumference gives about 21.11% under the historical formula. This percentage cannot be compared numerically with a waist-to-height ratio such as 0.500: they describe different outputs from different policies.

sections.title: Use the result as a transparent arithmetic check
paragraphs: Compare the inputs against the official worksheet, check the policy date and verify truncation before interpreting a discrepancy. If an official result differs, the assessment record and current service guidance take precedence over an online estimate.

Neither mode diagnoses health or prescribes a body composition target. For general circumference estimation outside this policy, the body-fat calculator explains its separate formulas and limitations.

army-body-fat-calculator.seoTitle: Army Body Fat Calculator: Waist-to-Height & Legacy Method

lean-body-mass-calculator.description: Compare lean-mass estimates from entered body fat, Boer, James, Hume or the pediatric Peters method, with equation-specific limits.

faqs.question: Is lean body mass the same as muscle mass?
faqs.answer: No. The non-fat compartment includes water, organs, bone and other tissues as well as muscle.

faqs.question: How do I calculate lean mass from body fat?
faqs.answer: Multiply weight by 1 minus the body-fat percentage divided by 100. For 70 kg and 20%, that is 70 × 0.80 = 56 kg.

faqs.question: Why does Boer disagree with my body-fat result?
faqs.answer: Boer uses height, weight and a sex coefficient; the other mode uses the supplied body-fat percentage. They have different predictors and uncertainties.

faqs.question: Can I use the adult equation for a child?
faqs.answer: Do not substitute the adult regression. A separate pediatric mode is provided with its own supported inputs and limitations.

faqs.question: Why might the James calculation be rejected?
faqs.answer: The formula can behave implausibly beyond its turning point. The calculator prevents use in that unsupported mathematical region.

faqs.question: Can I use the output for a medication dose?
faqs.answer: No. Medication dosing requires the relevant clinical protocol, assessment and professional judgment; these educational estimates do not establish a dose.

sections.title: Match the method to the information you actually have
paragraphs: If you have a body-fat estimate, the From body fat mode calculates lean mass directly from that percentage and body weight. The Boer mode instead estimates adult lean mass from height, weight and the equation’s sex coefficient. The pediatric Peters mode and historical James/Hume modes are separate methods with different populations and limitations.

An estimate of lean mass is not a measurement of muscle. It includes the non-fat compartment represented by the selected model. Comparing a body-fat calculation with an adult regression does not make either one a direct measurement.

sections.title: Worked example: 70 kg with an estimated 20% body fat
paragraphs: Lean mass = body weight × (1 − body-fat percentage / 100). At 70 kg and 20%, estimated fat mass is 14 kg and estimated lean mass is 56 kg. Enter 20 in the percentage field, not 0.20.

The input percentage controls the result directly. With body weight held at 70 kg, changing the estimate by two percentage points changes calculated lean mass by 1.4 kg. This illustrates sensitivity to the input; it is not evidence of an actual tissue change.

table.caption: Effect of the supplied percentage at the same 70 kg weight

sections.title: Reproduce the adult Boer estimate
paragraphs: The male equation is 0.407 × weight in kilograms + 0.267 × height in centimeters − 19.2. The female equation is 0.252 × weight + 0.473 × height − 48.3. For the male coefficients, 70 kg and 175 cm give 28.49 + 46.725 − 19.2 = 56.015 kg.
That close agreement with the 56 kg body-fat example is specific to these inputs. The regression does not use the 20% figure and will not generally reproduce a body-fat-based result.

sections.title: Keep pediatric and historical equations in context
paragraphs: The pediatric mode implements the Peters expression 3.8 × 0.0215 × weight(kg)^0.6469 × height(cm)^0.7236 within its supported age input of 2–14 years. At age 9, 30 kg and 135 cm, it gives about 25.66 kg. This is an educational body-composition estimate and must not be used to determine medication doses.

James uses a quadratic expression; at sufficiently high weight relative to height, its mathematical behavior becomes unsuitable. The historical mode rejects the unsupported turning-point region. Hume has its own original study population limits. An unavailable result is a reason to reconsider the method, not to change measurements until it accepts them.

links.label: Published pediatric equations in a pharmacokinetic study
